447: Built around Chosen, Masters of the Maelstrom, Defilers, Cultist Mobs, Abaddon, Huron Blackheart, and Vashtorr, this list runs both Cabal of Chaos and Fellhammer Siege-Host to stack a resilient mid-table gunline behind a mass horde screen. The plan is to flood objectives with Cultists while Chosen, Abaddon, and the Defilers grind through mid-board brawls, with Cabal's Dark Pact bonus Strength supercharging Psyker shooting and Fellhammer's wound-roll penalty making the whole army obnoxiously hard to crack with high-Strength ranged attacks. It punishes armies that rely on overloading a single target with big guns, since Fellhammer directly taxes wound rolls whenever Strength beats Toughness, blunting the most common anti-elite toolkit. Where it cracks is against low-Strength, high-volume firepower that stays under the Fellhammer threshold, or fast elite melee threats that can bypass the Cultist screen and isolate Abaddon and the Defilers before they stabilise.
448: Built around Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Vashtorr the Arkifane, and a Warpsmith support core, with Cultist Mobs screening the advance, this list floods the board with Heretic Astartes Daemon Vehicles all chasing Dark Pacts through the Soulforged Warpack detachment. The engine is straightforward: Vashtorr and the Warpsmith keep the daemon engines alive and operational while Dark Pacts fire up Soulforged Warpack's wound-roll bonus on ranged attacks and melee attack surge, turning every Venomcrawler and Defiler into a layered threat that punishes anything that lets them get their contracts off cleanly. This build absolutely shreds armoured lists — tanks, walkers, and vehicle-heavy armies face anti-armour overload across multiple activations with boosted wound rolls stacking onto already high-Strength platforms. The vulnerability is mortal wound spam and high-volume small-arms fire stripping wounds off multiple daemon engines simultaneously before Pacts can trigger, cracking the list open by killing its activations faster than the support core can compensate.
450: Built around Wyches, Incubi, Lady Malys, Drazhar, Lelith Hesperax, and a swarm of Venoms and Raiders, this is a mass-transport assault list running Exhibition Of Slaughter and Skysplinter Assault together — every disembark grants melee weapons Lance and ranged weapons Ignores Cover, while Wych Cult melee attacks carry Lethal Hits against non-Monsters and non-Vehicles. The win condition is a coordinated wave of transports crashing into midfield, disembarking elite killers with spiked damage profiles to delete priority targets and bury opponents in layered lethal output across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It punishes slower, high-toughness infantry armies that can't screen effectively, as the Lance-on-disembark interaction strips wound roll penalties while Lethal Hits bleeds through elite bodies efficiently. It cracks open against armies that can screen wide enough to deny clean disembark positions or alpha-strike the fragile transports before the assault wave ever lands.
466: Built around Flawless Blades, Tormentors, Infractors, and Lord Exultants flooding the board from Chaos Rhinos, with Lucius the Eternal, winged Daemon Princes, Noise Marines, and Defilers rounding out a mobile, infantry-heavy toolkit under the Mercurial Host and Spectacle of Slaughter detachments. The plan is to advance aggressively using Mercurial Host's re-roll, deliver Flawless Blades into combat where Spectacle of Slaughter grants them Fights First, then overwhelm mid-table objectives through sheer melee volume and Rhino-delivered pressure. It punishes slower, lower-model-count armies that can't handle simultaneous threats across multiple lanes, particularly lists that struggle to screen against fast infantry. Where it cracks is against high-volume shooting that strips Rhinos early and strands infantry in the open before the Fights First engine can engage.
473: Built around Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Terminator Squads, Grand Master Voldus, Brotherhood Chaplains, and supporting Strike and Interceptor Squads, this list runs the Argent Assault detachment to ensure Paladins wound up even when punching into high-Toughness targets. The win condition is layered melee pressure across multiple fronts — Paladins grind through elite infantry and monsters while Terminators, frequently supplemented by Hallowed Conclave's Fell Back and fight/shoot ability, contest and reclaim objectives without surrendering board presence after a bad combat. It punishes slow, durable armies that rely on Toughness to survive melee, since the core detachment strips that defensive buffer from Paladins entirely, and the mobile toolkit of Interceptors keeps the pressure spread wide. However, high-volume shooting lists that can strip Paladins before they engage, or armies that deny the melee phase through layered screens, crack this build open by neutering the wound-roll engine before it fires.
481: Built around the Knight Castellan and Knight Crusader, this list leans into the Dominus Foebreakers detachment's bonus to hit rolls against units in terrain, turning every defended objective into a killing ground for these massive Dominus-class walkers. The plan is to park overlapping fields of fire across the board, punish anything that goes to ground in cover, and grind down opposing armies through sheer volume of high-strength shooting — Archeotech Autoloaders supercharging output across the majority of lists. It absolutely brutalises gunline armies and dug-in elite infantry that rely on terrain saves, since the terrain-hit bonus strips the core defensive trade-off those builds depend on. However, fast melee threats that can close the distance and tie up the Castellans before they fire — or lists that screen aggressively to deny terrain clustering — can neutralise the detachment bonus and crack open what is ultimately a low-model-count army with limited redundancy.
480: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Armiger Helverins, a Knight Crusader, and a Knight Castellan, this list floods the table with medium and large walkers across every threat range. The plan is to apply relentless anti-armour pressure from multiple angles simultaneously — Helverins suppress at range while Warglaives chase down vehicles and monsters in melee, forcing opponents to split resources and concede priority targets. It punishes armour-heavy lists badly, stacking mobile anti-armour output that most vehicle-dense builds simply cannot absorb across multiple turns. Where it struggles is against elite infantry and screens: the list lacks the concentrated anti-horde volume to efficiently clear bodies off objectives, leaving it vulnerable to anything that can park cheap wounds in the way and deny scoring.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhl, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Hekaton Land Fortresses under the Hearthguard Covenant detachment, this is a brawling gunline that gets into your face at mid-range and stays there. The core engine is wound-reroll pressure within 9" — Hearthguard and Thunderkyn park close enough to trigger the detachment's wound-roll-of-1 rerolls, while Hekaton Land Fortresses and Kapricus Carriers deliver bodies forward and Hernkyn Pioneers screen flanks and contest secondaries. It punishes slow, durable infantry armies that can't dictate engagement range, because once the Hearthguard and Thunderkyn are within 9" the volume of re-rolled wounds overwhelms tough saves. Against highly mobile lists that can kite that 9" bubble or alpha-strike the Hearthguard before they close, the build loses its wound-reroll engine and the damage output drops sharply.
482: Built around Armiger Warglaives, a Knight Castellan, a Knight Crusader, Armiger Helverins, and a Cerastus Knight Lancer, this Freeblade Company list fields a full household of mixed-class Knights where every model benefits from Feel No Pain 6+ and ticks back a wound each Command phase — making every piece stubbornly durable across a long game. The win condition is mobile anti-armour saturation: closing fast with Lancers and Warglaives to crack hard targets while the Castellan and Crusader deliver sustained ranged firepower across every threat bracket. It punishes armies that rely on concentrated anti-tank to remove one threat at a time, because the wound-regeneration and FNP force opponents to overkill targets to actually delete them. Highly mobile elite armies that can contest objectives cheaply and avoid the Knight's guns — or lists that stack mortal wounds to bypass FNP entirely — expose the lack of cheap screening bodies and exploit the build's dependence on staying in range to matter.
456: Built around Technomancers, Canoptek Wraiths, Canoptek Reanimators, Canoptek Doomstalkers, and the Void Dragon, this is a highly mobile Canoptek Court machine that floods the board with durable constructs supported by layered repair and firepower. The win condition is controlling No Man's Land objective markers to unlock the Power Matrix across the mid-board, then grinding opponents down through a combination of resilient Wraith pressure and Doomstalker shooting while Technomancers — most carrying Dimensional Sanctum — keep key pieces alive. It punishes attrition-focused lists that expect to trade efficiently, as Reanimator-backed repair loops and persistent objective presence make the constructs genuinely difficult to fully clear. Armies that can alpha-strike the Technomancers off the board or flood cheap screening units to deny No Man's Land control early will undercut the Power Matrix engine before it ever comes online.
486: Built around nearly five squads of Boyz, multiple Painboyz, Ghazghkull Thraka, Warbosses, Bigbosses, Kommandos, Stormboyz, and Wazdakka Gutsmek operating under the Green Tide detachment, this is a wall of green flesh designed to suffocate the entire board. The win condition is volume attrition: Boyz units of 10+ models leverage their 5+ invulnerable save to stay on objectives long enough to grind opponents into dust through sheer model count and repeated combat phases. It punishes low-volume elite armies that lack the firepower to chew through multiple large Boyz blobs simultaneously while Painboyz keep them alive. Concentrated high-damage output that drops units below ten models collapses the invulnerable save threshold, and anything that clears screens efficiently before the horde makes contact can strip away the scoring engine before it gets rolling.
487: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, Beastboss characters, Kill Rigs, and Mozrog Skragbad, this is a mass-assault Beast Snagga force running Da Big Hunt to designate a priority Prey target each Command phase, letting the entire Beast Snagga contingent re-roll charges into it. The plan is to flood the midboard with bodies, nominate the most dangerous enemy piece as Prey, and crash Squighog Boyz and Kill Rigs into it with near-guaranteed charges while Gretchin and Boss Snikrot's infiltrating screens lock down objectives. It punishes elite low-body armies brutally — the sheer volume of charging bodies with re-roll charge insurance overwhelms anything that relies on staying out of melee range. Anything that can delete key beatstick characters at range before the first charge, or mass-remove Squighog Boyz with high-volume mortal output, bleeds the engine dry before it gets going.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan, two-plus Infernus Squads, Land Raider Redeemers, and Librarians running Forgefather's Seekers, this is a short-range flame-and-bolter gunline that delivers melta and fire through armoured transports. The engine is Seeker's Companions: Infernus Squads eligible to advance-and-shoot via the Assault bonus while Vulkan's presence pumps their Strength by 1 inside 12", turning mid-table engagements into a kill box that shreds infantry and light vehicles simultaneously. Librarians cycling Pyromancy or Divination disciplines stack hit-and-wound support onto already-loaded Infernus units, and Bladeguard Veterans with Adrax Agatone hold the objectives those transports just cleared. Armies that stay outside 12" or force long-range attrition strip away the Strength bonus and the whole kill-box premise, leaving an expensive midfield gunline exposed before it can close.
488: Built around multiple Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Flash Gitz, Tankbustas, and Big Mek Dakkariggs screened by waves of Gretchin and ferried by Trukks, this is a Dread Mob gunline that layers mechanised infantry pressure with a wall of high-volume firepower. The engine is Dread Mob's randomised weapon-ability table — selectively chosen via the alternative selection rule when stakes are high — amplifying Lootas and Shokk Attack Guns into fishing for devastating hits on hard targets while Tankbustas and Dakkariggs handle anti-armour overload. More Dakka! turns every ORKS INFANTRY unit into an Assault-capable threat, and when the Waaagh! fires up, Sustained Hits 1 across the board makes the sheer volume of shots punishing against anything without elite invulnerables or extreme damage mitigation. It cracks open midfield brawlers and vehicle-heavy lists that can't survive sustained multi-vector shooting, but tight melee assault armies that can close quickly and tie up the gunline before Dread Mob's abilities pay off will dismantle the relatively fragile screening Gretchin and collapse the firing line.
467: Built around Marneus Calgar in the Armour of Antilochus, Victrix Honour Guard, Repulsor Executioners, and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, this list runs the Blade of Ultramar detachment to cycle Combat Doctrines across the game — with Calgar on the table allowing reuse of already-selected Doctrines to keep buffs flowing turn after turn. The win condition is layered attrition: Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts hammer armour and infantry from range while Scouts, Intercessors, and Incursors hold objectives and screen, with Jump Pack Assault Intercessors threatening flanks and secondaries. It punishes slow, durable gunline armies that can't close the distance, overloading their damage budget across multiple hard targets simultaneously. It cracks under pressure from fast, high-volume alpha-strike lists that can strip the screening infantry early and isolate the big guns before Doctrine cycling generates enough return value.
428: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Riptides, Broadsides, Crisis Starscythes, Piranhas, and the Twin Lance, this is a mobile firepower army that moves and shoots without penalty across the first three battle rounds thanks to the Mont'ka detachment granting [ASSAULT] to all ranged weapons — then layers [LETHAL HITS] onto any Guided unit to punish armoured targets with lethal efficiency. The kill chain runs through Pathfinders providing Markerlights to Guided status, unlocking Lethal Hits on Riptides and Broadsides to crack heavy vehicles while Piranhas and Crisis suits harass flanks and contest mid-board objectives. It punishes slow, heavily armoured lists that rely on durability over evasion, since Lethal Hits combined with high-volume multi-damage shooting dismantles tough targets faster than they can reposition. Aggressive alpha-strike armies that close immediately and strip Pathfinder screens before Guided is established crack the scoring engine, and elite melee threats that survive the shooting phase can gut a T'au force with limited close-combat recourse.
483: Built around Norn Emissaries with Protean Purpose, Broodlord-led Genestealer blobs, Biovores, a Neurotyrant, Lictors, Tyrannofex, and Zoanthropes, this is a mobile toolbox army that floods the board with flexible, self-sufficient threats across every phase. The win condition is death by a thousand cuts — Genestealers and Lictors infiltrate to contest primary early while Biovore chip damage and Tyrannofex shooting pressure opponents off objectives, with Norn Emissaries flexing their Protean Purpose to fill whatever role the matchup demands. It punishes armies with spread-thin screens and low model counts, exploiting multiple simultaneous threat vectors that no single defensive answer can shut down. However, it struggles against elite gunlines and armies that can surgically delete Genestealer units before they connect, since losing that melee engine early leaves the rest of the list without a reliable close-in kill chain.
490: Built around Sekhetar Robots buffed by a dense psyker support network — Tzaangor Shamans and Exalted Sorcerers on Disc pushing Infusion auras to spike the Robots' melee WS — alongside Forgefiends and Defilers running Warpforged Cabal re-rolls to maximise vehicle shooting output. The plan is to park a psychic-tagged gunline of Robots and Forgefiends on mid-board objectives while Defilers and Daemon Princes threaten deep trades, letting the army score through staying power rather than a single kill chain. It punishes low-volume, high-toughness armies that struggle to cut through layered Psychic-keyed attacks and vehicle resilience propped up by repeated re-rolls on hit, wound, and damage. Armies that can strip the psyker bubble through ranged precision — sniping Shamans and Sorcerers before Infusion uptime pays off — collapse the melee threat envelope and leave the Robots swinging at reduced efficiency.
489: Built around Sorcerers in Terminator Armour leading Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Sekhetar Robots, foot Sorcerers, and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, this Hexwarp Thrallband list floods the table with bodies under the cover of the detachment's Flow of Magic — a persistent zone-control mechanic that rewards holding objectives in both your deployment zone and No Man's Land. The plan is to lock down mid-table early with Sekhetar Robots and Rubric screens, then layer sustained ranged pressure from Enlightened bows and Scarab Occult shooting while the Flow of Magic buffs activate phase by phase as objective control expands. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to contest multiple points simultaneously against this volume of durable infantry and robot chaff. Armies that alpha-strike the screening layer or apply high-AP anti-horde firepower to collapse the outer crust before Flow of Magic engages will expose the slower, less mobile core and shut down the scoring engine before it compounds.
427: Built around Crisis Sunforge and Starscythe Battlesuits, Coldstar Commanders, Commander Farsight, and The Twin Lance, this list floods the midboard with mobile battlesuit firepower backed by Kroot Carnivores and Vespid Stingwings as cheap objective screens. The win condition is a mid-to-late-game gunnery spike: Kauyon's Sustained Hits 1 and ignore-modifier Guided attacks from rounds three through five turn already-dangerous Crisis volleys into a deletion engine against anything Spotted by Pathfinders. Extended range from the detachment's Battlesuit Character ability lets Coldstars and Enforcers project threat without overextending, punishing static gunlines and elite armour that can't close the gap before Kauyon activates. The build cracks open against aggressive alpha-strike armies that collapse the Kroot screen early, denying the patient setup Kauyon demands and forcing Crisis units to trade unfavourably before they reach their damage ceiling.
484:
Built around Norn Assimilators, Norn Emissaries, Psychophages, Pyrovores, Biovores, and the Swarmlord, this is a regenerating meat-grinder that fields multiple massive monsters and keeps them alive through the Assimilation Swarm's Harvester heal mechanic, returning wounds and even destroyed infantry models every Command phase.

The win condition is attrition dominance: flood mid-table with bodies that refuse to die, leverage Protean Purpose on the Norn creatures to threaten multiple target profiles, and grind opponents into a scoring deficit through sheer resilience and board presence.

It punishes elite low-model-count lists that lack the sustained damage output to kill through regeneration fast enough, turning every inefficient damage roll into wasted activations.

It cracks open against mortal-wound spam and high-volume shooting that overwhelms the heal rate before it matters, and lists that ignore the monsters entirely to deny primary scoring leave the big creatures thrashing at nothing.
518: Built around Skorpekh Lords leading Skorpekh Destroyer blobs under Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit aura, the Void Dragon, Nekrosor Ammentar, Illuminor Szeras, the Silent King, and a Lokhust Lord shepherding Heavy Destroyers, this list floods the board with layered threats across every range band. The engine is relentless mid-board pressure: Awakened Dynasty's hit bonus supercharges Skorpekh melee packets while the Void Dragon and Heavy Destroyers crack armour from range, forcing opponents to answer multiple kill vectors simultaneously. It punishes lists that concentrate resources on a single threat type, since spreading anti-tank to stop the Destroyers leaves the Skorpekh wave untouched and vice versa. It struggles against armies that can deny its approach corridors or tarpit the Skorpekh units before they swing, bleeding the hit-bonus packets through screens before they reach their targets.
517: Built around paired Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, the Silent King, Technomancers, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list plays a mobile, multi-threat Necron package that leverages the Starshatter Arsenal's objective-proximity hit bonus to make every phase of its shooting deadlier the moment it contests ground. The win condition is sustained pressure: Doomsday Arks advance freely via Assault on their weapons, unloading at full effect while contesting objectives, while Wraiths, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers flood in from multiple angles to force opponents off markers and into unfavorable trades. It punishes static, vehicle-heavy armies that cluster around objectives by stacking lethal, repeated firepower into exactly those kill boxes. Highly mobile melee threats that can screen out the infiltrating units and kill the Arks before Technomancer reanimation kicks in will crack this list open.
530: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, Dawneagle Shield-Captains, Witchseekers, Allarus Shield-Captains, Custodian Wardens, Blade Champions, Custodian Guard, and Prosecutors operating under the Lions Of The Emperor detachment, this list weaponizes a single core rule: keep units isolated and every non-Vehicle attack gains +1 to hit and +1 to wound simultaneously. The win condition is spreading that buffed striking power across multiple independent threats — jetbikes harass flanks, Allarus drop into midfield, and infantry clusters hold objectives, each unit hunting alone to trigger the bonus and punish anything it touches. It excels against armies that cannot blanket the board with screens, because isolated elite units effortlessly find gaps and hit at a reliability tier most factions cannot match without specific defensive stacking. Armies that can force blob positioning — dense chaff screens, deep-strike denial, or tight zone control — suppress the isolation bonus and expose how few wounds Custodes bodies actually bring per point spent.
525: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Sammael, Lion El'Jonson, the Ravenwing Command Squad, Outrider Squads, and Azrael, this is an all-in mobile gunline that leans hard into the Company of Hunters detachment's ability to Advance-and-shoot or fall-back-and-shoot across every MOUNTED unit, while Darkflight Pursuit strips cover from virtually everything the Ravenwing FLY units target. The win condition is overwhelming mobile anti-armour pressure — speeders and Thunderstrikes reposition freely each turn, keeping guns on priority targets while Scouts and Intercessors hold objectives cheaply behind the skimmer wall. It punishes slow, durable gunlines and heavy-armour-dependent lists by denying safe positioning and applying layered lethality that can't easily be screened. Highly mobile alpha-strike lists or armies with strong assault units that can force multiple combats simultaneously expose its relatively fragile chassis, tying up speeders in melee and switching off the advance-and-shoot engine.
529: Built around Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Logan Grimnar, Ragnar Blackmane, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wolf Guard Terminators, and a dense screen of Grey Hunters, Blood Claws, and Wolf Scouts operating under Saga of the Beastslayer, this is a mass-infantry brawler that layers Lethal Hits on every attack targeting Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles while flooding the board with cheap bodies. The plan is to complete the Beastslayer tally early — killing enough enemy units to unlock army-wide Lethal Hits — then crash a wave of mid-table melee threats backed by character buffs from Battle Leaders and Wolf Priests into the opponent's scoring pieces. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that rely on a few expensive Characters or Vehicles, since Lethal Hits on every swing makes those units bleed far faster than expected. Horde mirrors and high-volume shooting lists that ignore the Beastslayer threshold entirely will crack this open, since the army's durability is shallow and the Lethal Hits payoff diminishes sharply against cheap-infantry targets.
521: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Ghostkeels, Riptides, Broadsides, and Commander Shadowsun operating under Advanced Acquisition Cadre and Kauyon, this list leans on hidden shooting — Stealth Battlesuits and Pathfinder Teams fire without breaking concealment — then transitions into a Kauyon-fueled late-game firepower spike from rounds three through five, where everything gains Sustained Hits 1 and Guided units ignore modifiers when targeting Spotted enemies. The win condition is attrition: screen with Piranhas and Vespid Stingwings to deny forward pressure, accumulate mid-game objective presence, and then overwhelm with amplified shooting once Kauyon activates. It punishes slow, durable armour-heavy lists by combining mobile anti-armour tools with the late-round damage multiplier to crack tough targets that other armies would stall against. Lists that alpha-strike the screening layer early or flood the midboard before Kauyon comes online deny it the time it needs to snowball.
441: Built around Azrael, multiple Librarians (including Librarian in Terminator Armour), Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and a supporting mass of Scouts, Intercessors, and Sternguard Veterans under the Librarius Conclave detachment, with roughly three-quarters of lists also running Unforgiven Task Force to maintain Objective Control under pressure. The engine is the Librarius Conclave's round-by-round Psychic Discipline selection — Divination for rerolling hit and wound rolls of 1 on priority targets, Biomancy to push elite melee units into threatening range, Pyromancy for board-clear — layering that flexibility onto hard-hitting elite infantry and a deep gunline of Sternguard. It punishes slower, durable elite armies that can't contest the midboard, where heavy screening infantry and elevated OC from Unforgiven Task Force lock down objectives while the Terminator-armoured core grinds through anything that closes. The build cracks when fast, high-volume alpha-strike lists bypass its screens before the Discipline engine can cycle, or when concentrated anti-tank overload removes its Terminator blocks before they reach engagement range.
550: Built around multiple Lords of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, Be'lakor, and Flamers and Screamers as mobile threat packages, this list runs the Lords Of The Warp detachment — boosting non-monster Characters to higher Leadership and OC — and layers in the Scintillating Legion's Flux token re-rolls to squeeze consistency from its Tzeentch units across every dice phase. The plan is to flood midfield with fast, lethal bodies: Screamers contest and harass, Flamers torch infantry, and the Lords of Change plus Kairos apply overwhelming psychic-and-shooting pressure while the Character OC bonus lets them personally hold objectives without ceding ground. It punishes static, infantry-heavy lists that can't keep pace with the board-wide mobility or answer multiple large flying threats simultaneously. Dedicated high-volume anti-air or elite melee that can isolate and delete individual Lords of Change will crack it open, since the whole threat matrix depends on those expensive centerpiece models surviving.
551: Built around Flesh Hounds, Skarbrand, Bloodcrushers, Bloodletters, Rendmasters on Blood Throne, a Bloodthirster, and Bloodmaster characters, with Nurglings and Plaguebearers providing durable filler screening, this is a Blood Legion surge-pressure list that weaponises the detachment's reactive movement — each time an enemy unit ends a move within 8" of a Khorne Daemon unit, one of those units lurches forward D6" — to collapse the gap and deliver multiple lethal combat threats simultaneously. The win condition is stacking Khorne charges across several fronts at once so the opponent cannot absorb them all, while Nurglings and Plaguebearers contest objectives and eat removal that would otherwise clear the attack packages. It punishes slower, combat-averse armies that must reposition frequently, because every enemy move triggers another surge opportunity that compounds the threat radius. Ranged armies that can force fall-backs, reset spacing, and pick apart the horde before it converges will crack the list, since there is almost no shooting with which to punish passive play.
459: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, Leman Russ variants (Battle Tank and Exterminator), Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this is a mechanised armoured column running the Designation Force detachment, where Scout Sentinels and Infantry Smoke units plant Signal Flares to paint targets for the rest of the fleet. The win condition is layered designation fire: Sentinels sprint forward to mark high-value threats, then the massed Squadron guns delete them from the gunline, with Hellhounds covering flanks and burning out infantry screens that would otherwise block line of sight. This build punishes armour-heavy and elite lists brutally — stacking Squadron volume fire against expensive targets it has already designated strips even durable vehicles efficiently. It cracks open against fast aggressive armies that can swamp the Sentinels before flares land, collapsing the designation chain and leaving the static gunline shooting blind into a melee it cannot escape.
465: Built around daemonettes, defilers, lords exultant, infractors, tormentors, and chaos rhinos operating under the Carnival of Excess detachment, this list floods the midboard with Empowered units — Emperor's Children and Legions of Excess models granting each other Sustained Hits when within 6" — while rhinos deliver infractors and tormentors directly into the fight. The win condition is a coordinated mid-table brawl where the Empowered aura chains across multiple units simultaneously, generating overwhelming volume of hits to grind through anything in range. It punishes horde-adjacent lists and anything that wants to trade attrition in the open, where defilers provide mobile anti-armour punch and daemonette mass drowns screens. It cracks against armies that can deny the 6" Empowered bubble through long-range threat or aggressive dispersion, forcing units to fight piecemeal and without Sustained Hits.
546:
Built around the Void Dragon, the Nightbringer, Immortals, and Flayed Ones under the Hand of the Dynasty detachment, this list fields multiple god-tier monsters backed by a flexible, mobile infantry core whose Assault-granted ranged attacks let them advance and shoot without sacrificing actions.

The plan is to use the C'tan as devastating threat vectors that demand immediate answers while Immortals and Flayed Ones flood objectives and complete actions simultaneously, stretching the opponent's removal across too many high-value targets.

Slower, tightly packed armies struggle most here, as the C'tan's raw staying power and the Flayed Ones' board presence punish lists that can't efficiently prioritize which monster to remove first.

The build cracks when opponents can concentrate elite anti-monster firepower and reduce the C'tan quickly, leaving the infantry screen holding objectives with limited damage output to contest back.
544: Built around multiple Skorpekh Lord-led Skorpekh Destroyer units, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Nekrosor Ammentar, Illuminor Szeras, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers under Lokhust Lords, the Silent King, and Ophydian Destroyers, this Awakened Dynasty list weaponizes the detachment's +1 to Hit across nearly every combat and shooting unit on the table. The win condition is layered threat saturation — Ophydians and Skorpekhs hunt infantry midboard while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers and the Void Dragon crack vehicles, with Enaegic Dermal Bond keeping lead characters alive long enough to cycle damage into scoring turns. It punishes lists with spread-out, mid-toughness targets that can't absorb simultaneous melee and heavy anti-armour pressure from multiple angles. Concentrated alpha-strike armies or elite high-damage output can strip the attached characters before the hit-bonus engine fires, unraveling the whole threat package.
526: Built around Lokhust Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Lychguard, and the Overlord with Translocation Shroud, this is a multi-vector Necron murder machine that floods the board with fast, durable threat vectors across multiple phases. The plan is to overwhelm opponents by projecting lethal ranged pressure through Lokhust Destroyers and the Void Dragon while Ophydian Destroyers threaten sudden melee eruptions from unexpected angles, forcing opponents to defend multiple kill zones simultaneously rather than concentrating resources. Its high mobility toolkit punishes slower, static gunlines that can't reposition quickly enough to address threats from all directions at once. It cracks open against tight alpha-strike armies and anything capable of stripping the Lokhust Destroyers before they activate, since losing that ranged backbone early collapses the layered threat structure the entire plan depends on.
556: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Mozrog Skragbad, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Squighog Boyz, and Beast Snagga Boyz, this is a War Horde wall of melee muscle backed by Gretchin screens, Boyz blobs, and Painboy support — every Ork model swinging with Sustained Hits 1 across the board. The win condition is a coordinated mid-board brawl where overlapping melee threats force opponents to trade into multiple dangerous units simultaneously, with Follow Me Ladz and Trukk-delivered infantry accelerating the crash and Wazdakka providing mobile pressure to dictate engagement timing. It punishes gunline and elite low-model-count armies brutally — the sheer volume of Sustained Hits 1 attacks overwhelms anything that can't clear dozens of wounds per turn. It cracks against opponents with reliable high-AP shooting or board control that can peel screens before the main wave connects, leaving the heavies exposed and overcosted for what they accomplish.
558: Built around Wazdakka Gutsmek, massed Warbikers, Deffkoptas, Deffkilla Wartrikes, Gretchin screens, and Trukks, this is a Kult of Speed army — most lists run the detachment that lets Speed Freeks shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back, turning the entire force into a relentless, always-threatening tide of fast biker violence. The plan is to flood mid-table from turn one, keep every unit eligible to fight or shoot regardless of movement, and grind opponents off objectives through sheer weight of attacks and bodies rather than any single kill spike. It punishes static or short-ranged armies badly — a list that needs to stand still or weather an approach gets crashed into repeatedly by units that never lose offensive output for repositioning. It cracks under elite long-range firepower that can strip bikers wholesale before they close, or against hard anti-horde tools that collapse the Gretchin screens early and leave the fast elements overexposed.
533: Built around multiple Commanders in Coldstar Battlesuits, Crisis Sunforge and Starscythe Battlesuits, The Twin Lance, Commander Farsight, Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams with Darkstrider, Broadsides, and Crisis Fireknife Battlesuits running Experimental Prototype Cadre plus Kauyon — every Battlesuit Character's guns reach 6" further, and from round three onward the whole force gains Sustained Hits 1 plus the ability to ignore modifiers when Guided units target Spotted enemies. The plan is to spend early turns screening and positioning while Pathfinders spot targets, then detonate into a mid-table brawl from round three when Kauyon activates, stacking Sustained Hits 1 onto high-volume anti-armour Crisis and Coldstar payloads to delete hard targets and bury opponents in VP. It punishes durable, low-model-count elite armies that want to trade units slowly, because the Sustained Hits surge turns already efficient anti-armour firepower into an overload their saves cannot absorb. Armies that alpha strike before round three or flood the board with cheap screens crack it open, denying the Kauyon payoff window and blocking Pathfinder spot-chains before they mature.
561: Built around Sorcerers in Terminator Armour leading Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Tzaangors, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, and Sekhetar Robots, this Rubricae Phalanx list fields a dense, layered infantry horde that floods the board with bodies across multiple unit types. The detachment's core rule adds 1 to armour saves against any attack with an unmodified Damage 1 characteristic, making Rubricae models a nightmare to chip down with small-arms, so the plan is to park durable units on objectives while Fatecaster Greatbow Enlightened and Sekhetar Robots apply skimmer fire pressure to force bad trades. It punishes lists reliant on high-volume, low-damage shooting — those guns bounce off the damage-1 save modifier and bleed CP or fail to shift the horde before scoring windows close. It cracks open against high-damage multi-wound weapons that sidestep the save bonus entirely, or elite melee that can carve through Terminator and Tzaangor blobs before attrition works in the Phalanx's favour.
560: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Sekhetar Robots buffed by Sorcerers (including Terminators), Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Daemon Princes, and Magnus the Red, this list runs the Hexwarp Thrallband detachment to project a Flow of Magic across No Man's Land whenever it controls half the midfield objectives, unlocking army-wide Psychic synergies — and pairs it with Sekhetar Cohort to grant Robots Psychic attacks and WS buffs from nearby Psykers. The win condition is layered, simultaneous pressure: Robots and Terminators brawl for midfield markers to trigger and sustain Flow of Magic while Enlightened and gunline elements delete screens, forcing opponents into no-win trades. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot contest multiple objectives simultaneously against this volume of Psychic-tagged melee and ranged threat across every zone. It cracks open against fast alpha-strike lists that can collapse midfield control early and sever Flow of Magic before the kill engine comes online.
571: Built around Skitarii Rangers, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Skorpius Disintegrators, Sicarian Infiltrators and Ruststalkers, Kastelan Robots, and Belisarius Cawl directing the whole machine, this Eradication Cohort force pairs a layered gunline with aggressive midfield brawlers transported into position aboard Skorpius Duneriders. The plan is to use Cawl and Marshal-spread Imperative buffs — re-rolling 1s to hit or wound depending on the active Imperative — to grind down mid-table threats while Sicarians and Kastелans punch into objectives and hold them through sheer durability. It punishes static or low-mobility armies that can't disengage from the Sicarian threat packages flooding into their midfield. However, elite melee forces that can crack the transports early and alpha-strike the fragile Skitarii cores before Imperatives stabilize will expose how brittle this army becomes without its positioning scaffolding.
609: Built around Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Allarus Custodians, Blade Champion, Vertus Praetors, Contemptor-Achillus Dreadnoughts, and Telemon Heavy Dreadnoughts, this list runs the Might of the Moritoi detachment to give every Walker +2" Movement and +1 to advance and charge rolls, turning already-imposing Dreadnoughts into terrifying threat-range engines. The plan is to flood multiple angles simultaneously — fast Walkers crashing into melee while Vertus Praetors harass flanks — forcing opponents to split resources and exposing whichever combat unit gets ignored. The Shield Host Ka'tah rotation layering Critical Hits or improved AP on top of elite melee profiles punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot screen multiple simultaneous charges. Lists built around static gunlines or fragile objective campers struggle most, but anything with durable chaff screens and strong anti-tank shooting can stall the Walker momentum before it ever connects.
584: Built around Krieg Combat Engineers, Tempestus Scions with Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Gaunt's Ghosts, Scout Sentinels, Krieg Heavy Weapons Squads, Cadian Recon Squads, Cadian Shock Troops, and Taurox transports, this is a mass-infantry gunline running the Designation Force detachment, with just over half of lists adding Siege Regiment's Creeping Barrage to punish distant enemy units with Shaken. The win condition is layering Signal Flares from Scout Sentinels and Sentinels onto priority targets, saturating them with coordinated small-arms and heavy weapons fire while a horde of cheap bodies contests objectives across the board. It punishes infantry-heavy lists through sheer volume of fire and attrition, denying movement with Creeping Barrage while Scions and Engineers apply focused pressure. It struggles against elite low-model-count armies that can methodically delete its key pieces before the numbers game overwhelms them.
610: Built around witchseekers, custodian guard, custodian wardens, blade champion, prosecutors, and allarus custodians operating under the Talons of the Emperor detachment, this is an elite combined-arms force blending Adeptus Custodes durability with Anathema Psykana screening elements. The win condition is layered attrition across multiple threat vectors — witchseekers and prosecutors screen and deny opponent actions while Custodian squads and allarus custodians pressure objectives, with the Null Aegis aura providing psychic and mortal wound resilience that keeps the core alive long enough to outscore through sustained presence. It punishes psyker-heavy and mortal-wound-reliant lists brutally, as the Null Aegis bubble functionally neutralises those damage sources across wide swaths of the board. However, high-volume conventional shooting or anti-tank overload from mechanised lists can strip the relatively small model count before the elite infantry's durability advantage pays off.
542: Built around Noise Marines ferried in Chaos Rhinos, Chaos Bikers, Cultist Mobs, Chosen, Red Corsairs Raiders, a Lord Discordant on Helstalker, Defilers, and led by Huron Blackheart and Masters of the Maelstrom, this is a Renegade Raiders list that floods the board with mobile, shoot-on-the-move firepower. The engine is simple but punishing: Renegade Raiders grants every Heretic Astartes ranged weapon the Assault ability and sharpens AP by 1 when shooting near objectives, so disembarking Noise Marines and advancing Bikers blast apart anything contesting a marker while scoring simultaneously. It hammers gunline and static armies that cannot deny objective presence, because the AP bonus stacks with the sheer volume of shots pouring in from multiple angles across mid-board. However, fast aggressive armies that can strip the Rhino transports early or pin the horde in deployment deny the advance tempo this list depends on entirely.
471: Built around Knight Despoilers, War Dog Karnivores, and dense screens of Nurglings and Beasts of Nurgle, this is a Nurgle-flavoured Infernal Lance warband that floods the board with resilient chaff while projecting massive anti-armour threat through its towering walkers. The engine is Malefic Surge Empowerment — risking mortal wounds each Command phase to unlock enhanced offensive output on Despoilers and Karnivores, letting them crack elite armour and monsters while Nurglings and Beasts contest objectives and absorb return fire. It punishes slow, armour-heavy lists that can't clear through layered screening infantry before the Knights close and deliver overwhelming melee and ranged anti-tank pressure. Armies with high-volume mortal wound output or strong melee denial can strip the screening layer fast and strand the Knights on bad ground, exposing their Leadership dependency.
595: Built around Indomitor Kill Teams, Deathwatch Veterans, Terminator squads, a Captain in Gravis Armour, and the Watch Master, this is a mixed-profile gunline that leans hard into the Black Spear Task Force's wound-reduction mechanic — blended Toughness units force opponents to wound against the majority value, making kill teams surprisingly durable against shooting. The plan is to park bodies on objectives and grind through raw volume of fire against hordes and light armour while the Terminators and Veterans threaten mid-board control. It punishes mass-infantry lists and gunlines that rely on weight of attacks at a single Toughness bracket, as the mixed-model wound calculation blunts efficiency and forces opponents into awkward targeting. High-density elite lists and alpha-strike armies crack it open by bypassing the wound-reduction tech entirely with precise, high-damage elite units that don't care about majority Toughness thresholds.
575: Built around Hellions, Wyches, Incubi, Reavers, and a dense Venom fleet, this is a mass-infantry Wych Cult list that floods the board with cheap bodies disembarking from skimmers. Exhibition Of Slaughter grants all Wych Cult melee attacks Lethal Hits against non-Monster/Vehicle targets, turning every chaff brawl into a delete button — Wyches and Hellions pile into screens and infantry blobs and simply erase them while Scourges handle armor from range. It punishes elite-infantry lists ruthlessly, where Lethal Hits compound across multiple units and the sheer volume of attacks overwhelms save efficiency. It cracks against heavy armored armies and anything with durable Monsters or Vehicles, since the Lethal Hits clause explicitly excludes those target types, leaving the melee engine underperforming against the hardest targets on the table.
541: Built around Warp Talons, Chaos Lords with Jump Packs, Raptors, Defilers, Chosen, Red Corsairs Raiders, and Cultist Mobs screening the flanks, this is a mobile assault list that floods the mid-board with flying infantry and daemon engines. The core engine is attrition-through-pressure: Cultists contest objectives and absorb casualties while Warp Talons and Raptors dive onto weakened or battle-shocked enemy units, triggering re-roll-1s to hit from Murdertalon Raiders and turning already-struggling opponents into free kills. It punishes slow gunlines and horde armies hard, using superior mobility to isolate units below half-strength, stack the detachment's hit debuff on counter-attackers, and bury opponents under cumulative chip damage. However, it cracks against aggressive alpha-strike lists that can one-round the Cultist screens before the flying infantry engage, leaving the hammer without an anvil and the Warp Talons exposed before they can leverage their conditional bonuses.
588: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Lord Exultants, Tormentors, Lucius the Eternal, winged Daemon Princes, Defilers, and Noise Marines — with Rhinos ferrying infantry into contact — this is a charge-or-die melee army running Peerless Bladesmen, where every successful charge unlocks either Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 across the attacking unit, and Spectacle of Slaughter grants Flawless Blades Fights First to punish overwatch or counter-charge attempts. The win condition is coordinated multi-unit charges: pile Rhino-delivered infantry onto mid-board objectives, trigger the charge bonus across multiple units simultaneously, and erase whatever holds the ground. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb multiple Lethal Hits charge waves without crumbling, and whose counter-melee options are too slow to respond. However, lists with durable shooting, strong screens, or deep-strike denial can strand the Rhinos short and neutralise the charge bonus entirely before a single blade swings.
592: Built around Castellan Crowe, multiple Purifier Squads, and a double-stack of Nemesis Dreadknights alongside Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, this list floods the board with elite infantry supported by heavy walker firepower. The win condition is expanding Hallowed Ground — the detachment's territorial mechanic — by pushing Purifiers into No Man's Land to contest objectives and unlock additional coverage, while the Dreadknights provide the kill power to hold that ground and punish counterplay. It thrives against infantry-heavy lists that rely on objective presence, because layered lethality from Dreadknight melee and Purifier shooting systematically collapses screens before they can deny ground. Armies that can reliably alpha-strike the Dreadknights at range or outrange the Purifiers' threat bubble crack this open, leaving Hallowed Ground starved and the scoring engine stalled.
591: Built around Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Terminator Squads, Purgation Squads, Strike Squads, and a Grand Master supported by a Brotherhood Librarian, this is a transport-heavy elite infantry list that floods the board with Psychic melee and shooting threats across Razorback-delivered packages. The engine is Argent Assault's wound-roll buff keeping Paladins dangerous into high-Toughness targets, layered with Banishers' Leadership-gated Sustained Hits on melee weapons to spike damage output when the squad hits combat. It punishes mid-tier elite armies that can't clear durable Terminator bodies efficiently, using volume of Psychic attacks and mobile repositioning to contest every objective simultaneously. It cracks under concentrated high-volume anti-infantry firepower or elite melee that beats it to the punch before the Leadership tests and wound buffs come online.
594: Built around packs of Armiger Warglaives and Armiger Helverins, this list uses the Gate Warden Lance to anchor two foundation objectives, establishing a defensive line while flooding the board with fast, hard-hitting Armigers. The win condition is controlling that defensive corridor while Bondsman-buffed Armigers apply Ignores Cover ranged pressure — Helverins strip armour at range, Warglaives clean up in melee, and the foundation markers make scoring your home objectives nearly automatic. It punishes elite armoured lists hard, layering mobile anti-tank volume that forces opponents to trade inefficiently into multiple Armiger threats simultaneously. Its weakness is scoring outside the defensive line against aggressive objective-flooding armies, and high-volume mortal wound output or anti-infantry spam can strip any soft screens it relies on to protect the big Knights in about a third of lists.
580: Built around Doomsday Arks, Flayed Ones, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, and the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, this list plants heavy artillery in a protected backfield castle while mobile threats roam forward to threaten objectives and key targets. The Doomsday Arks anchor the firebase, layering anti-tank firepower from range while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers add concentrated armour-cracking shots, and the Nightbringer threatens anything that pushes into midfield. Flayed Ones provide aggressive board pressure and objective harassment, forcing opponents to either overcommit to chasing them or cede ground to the castle. The build punishes slow, durable armies that want to grind forward into ranged fire, but aggressive alpha-strike lists that close distance quickly can outpace the damage output and crack the firebase before the heavy guns can answer.
604: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Warbosses, Boyz, Nobz, Stormboyz, and Breaka Boyz hauled forward in Trukks and Battlewagons, this is a War Horde list that puts Sustained Hits 1 on every Ork melee weapon in the army. The plan is to deliver overlapping waves of infantry into combat simultaneously — transports crack the midboard open while Stormboyz and Boss Snikrot's infiltrators pin or delete screens, letting the main blob swarm objectives and grind opponents into paste through sheer volume of Sustained attacks. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb the volume of melee dice, especially when Ghazghkull and Follow Me Ladz keep key units punching above their weight. Armies that can alpha strike the transports before they unload, or that have durable shooting to attrit the hordes at range, can strip the engine before it gets into contact.
601: Built around massed Boyz squads, multiple Warbosses, Ghazghkull Thraka, Painboys keeping bodies alive, and Big Mek Dakkarigs and Wazdakka Gutsmek rounding out the command structure, this is a War Horde list that blankets the table with green bodies and charges everything into melee, where every Ork model's weapons gain Sustained Hits 1. The win condition is simple attrition: flood objectives with sheer model count, crash Ghazghkull and Warboss-buffed Boyz into whatever is holding them, and generate extra hits in combat until the opponent runs out of ways to clear the board. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't efficiently trade into hordes — if the opposing list needs two or three attacks to kill each Boy, the math rapidly collapses in the Orks' favour. The weakness is high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that bypass the Painboy's healing and delete entire squads before they reach combat, cracking the mass-body engine before Sustained Hits 1 ever comes online.
605: Built around Meganobz, Nobz, multiple Warbosses (including Ghazghkull Thraka and a Warboss in Mega Armour), and Painboys hauling forward in Trukks and Battlewagons, this is a transport-infantry brawler that floods the midboard with elite melee threats backed by a deep Boyz and Gretchin screen. The engine is the double-Waaagh! — the detachment lets a second Waaagh! fire specifically for Warboss, Nobz, and Meganobz units, letting you crash an already-buffed murder-wave into the opponent's face twice across the game while Painboys keep the blobs alive long enough to score on contact. It punishes slow, fragile, or low-model-count armies that can't absorb repeated waves of powered-up melee, especially those without reliable board-wide screening to slow the transports down. Anything with high-volume shooting that can strip Trukks early and strand the cargo in the open before the Waaagh! window arrives will crack this list before it gets its hands dirty.
602: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Painboyz, and dense waves of Gretchin, Boyz, Lootas, Tankbustas, and Flash Gitz ferried in Trukks, this is a Freebooter Krew gunline-brawler hybrid that blankets the board in bodies and bullets. The plan is to lock down the loot objective each Command phase while Sustained Hits 1 on every attack — triggered across Infantry, Mounted, and Walkers — turns the sheer volume of Ork shooting into a murderous numbers game that bleeds opponents dry mid-table. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't clear hordes fast enough, as Painboyz keep key units alive long enough to contest and overwhelm. It cracks open against fast, high-mobility lists that can isolate and delete Trukks before they unload, stranding expensive units out of position and collapsing the firepower engine.
598: Built around Hyperadapted Raveners, Raveners, The Red Terror, and Trygon emerging from underground alongside Biovores, Zoanthropes, Neurotyrant, The Swarmlord, Hormagaunts, Von Ryan's Leapers, Lictors, and Neurolictors, this Subterranean Assault list is a multi-wave burrowing swarm that floods the midboard from every angle. The win condition is simultaneous pressure — Burrower units spike out of the ground into melee while Biovores and Zoanthropes provide backfield fire support, overwhelming opponents who can only respond to one threat at a time. It punishes static gunlines and elite low-model-count armies that lack the bodies to screen every emergence point, forcing impossible choices across multiple objective zones. It cracks open when faced with deep-strike denial and layered screening that collapses the emergence windows, or massed high-AP shooting that kills the fragile synapse web before the swarm can coordinate.
607: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines (averaging 2.5 squads), Scarab Occult Terminators, a Winged Daemon Prince, Sorcerers, Tzaangors, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Sekhetar Robots, and Chaos Rhinos running under the Grand Coven detachment, this is a layered psychic shooting army with a dense, mobile infantry core. The win condition is cycling Grand Coven's command-phase abilities — most critically the range extension on psychic weapons and the damage amplification pulse — to create kill windows where Rubric Marines and Enlightened deliver lethal volleys from unexpected distances while Magnus and the Daemon Prince threaten key targets in melee. Rhino-mounted Rubrics enable aggressive mid-board presence, and the sheer volume of bodies across Tzaangors and Chaos Spawn punishes elite low-model armies that cannot efficiently answer both the horde screen and the hard-hitting characters simultaneously. It cracks under sustained anti-infantry area denial and armies that can neutralize Magnus early, since losing that anchor collapses the offensive output the rest of the list is designed to amplify.
485: Built around Norn Emissaries, Norn Assimilators, Maleceptors, Tyrannofexes, Exocrines, Biovores, and the Swarmlord, this list fields an almost entirely Monster-keyword army that leverages Crusher Stampede's Objective Control bonus — healthy units at Starting Strength contribute +2 OC — while threatening firepower across every range band. The win condition is board control through OC saturation: park full-strength Monsters on objectives to lock out scoring, then use the Talons of the Norn Queen's Protean Purpose ability on Norn Emissaries and Assimilators to flex into whatever threat profile the matchup demands. It punishes slow, elite armies that can't kill multiple large-bodied units per turn, because degrading a Monster only makes it hit and wound harder under Crusher Stampede's enrage bonus. It cracks against mass-fire gunlines or alpha-strike lists that can spike multiple Monsters below half-strength early, collapsing both OC dominance and board presence simultaneously.
565: Built around Jakhals screening for waves of Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, Slaughterbound, Defilers, and Forgefiends, with a Daemon Prince of Khorne threading the aggression together, this is a Brazen Engines list that floods the midboard with Daemon Vehicles whose Terror of Khorne ability forces battle-shock rolls on anything they engage in melee. The plan is layered mobile pressure — Forgefiends strip light armour at range while the Eightbound variants and Defilers crash into whatever survives, with Jakhals buying time and absorbing screens to clear lanes. It punishes slower, mid-density armies that can't prevent multiple simultaneous engagements, using the battle-shock cascade to collapse defensive coherence before the fight phase concludes. Balanced shooting lists that can pick apart the infantry screen and then kite the slower Daemon Vehicles will expose the plan's reliance on getting everything into contact at once.
719: Built around Repentia Squads, Arco-Flagellants, Celestian Sacresants, and Rhino transports, this list floods the board with waves of fanatical melee infantry delivered by Penitent Host's rotating Vows of Atonement — cycling movement boosts and fight-phase buffs each round — while Sacred Champions sharpens the Sacresants to hit on elite accuracy. The win condition is overwhelming close-combat volume: Rhinos deliver Repentia and Arco-Flagellants into threat range, Triumph of Saint Katherine and Hospitaller keep bodies alive through attrition, and Intranzia Fraye amplifies the kill chain. It punishes slow, static armies that can't screen against multiple simultaneous assault threats arriving from transports. It cracks open when faced with alpha-strike shooting that strips Rhinos before they deliver their cargo, leaving fragile infantry exposed in the open.
710: Built around Witchseekers, Prosecutors, and a wall of Custodes Dreadnoughts — Achillus, Galatus, Telemon, and Venerable Contemptors — backed by Caladius Grav-Tanks, this Silent Hunters list runs the Solar Spearhead secondary detachment to inflate vehicle Objective Control while healthy and sustain accuracy when damaged. The plan is to use Ceaseless Vigilance to null priority targets, then bury them under layered lethal firepower from multiple dreadnought chassis and grav-tank salvos while Anathema Psykana infantry advance and still complete actions. It punishes lists that rely on small elite units or exposed vehicles, as the combination of nulling and concentrated multi-vector shooting systematically dismantles anything that clusters or presents clear priority targets. It cracks under aggressive alpha strikes and high-volume screening armies, where losing vehicles before they can leverage full Starting Strength OC collapses the objective game entirely.
717: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Celestian Sacresants, Arco-Flagellants, and a deep bench of infantry packed into Immolators and Castigators, this list plays the full Hallowed Martyrs engine: every unit that takes casualties hits harder, so the ideal game state is controlled attrition rather than avoiding damage. The win condition is deliberately feeding units into combat and gunfire until they drop below Starting Strength, then unleashing the detachment's +1 to Hit — and once Below Half-strength, +1 to Wound as well — turning wounded remnants into over-performing killers that punch well above their remaining bodies. Celestian Insidiants threatening flanks while Immolators deliver fresh infantry punishes gunline armies that spread damage thinly across many units, triggering the wound bonus across the board simultaneously. The build cracks when opponents can delete units cleanly before the martyrdom bonus activates, denying the feedback loop entirely and leaving expensive warsuit bodies with no payoff.
662: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Kasrkin, Gaunt's Ghosts, Krieg Combat Engineers, Scout Sentinels, and Cadian Shock Troops, this Bridgehead Strike list plays a deep-strike gunline that floods the board with elite infantry dropping from reserve. The win condition is landing Scions and Command Squads on turn to trigger the detachment's +1 to hit on arrival, then dumping concentrated hot-shot and special-weapon volleys into priority targets before the opponent can respond. It punishes static gunlines and heavy-armour lists by combining mobile anti-armour output with mass bodies that contest objectives through Battleline Scions' boosted OC. However, it struggles against fast aggressive armies that can either intercept the drop zones or overwhelm the relatively fragile infantry screen before the alpha-strike pays off.
693: Built around Crusade Ancients, Crusader Squads, Execrators, Scout Squads, Chaplain Grimaldus, Intercessors, and Bladeguard Veterans, this Vindication Task Force list floods the board with massed infantry screened behind Ancient-anchored durability — the Wound-roll subtraction on Ancient units sitting on objectives makes the core blocks punishingly hard to shift off scoring ground. The win condition is attrition-through-presence: hold every mid-table objective with overlapping Ancient bubbles and Grimaldus supporting nearby, then grind opposing units down while banking primary points every round. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that rely on high-Strength shooting to clear objectives efficiently, since the wound-roll penalty blunts exactly that removal tool. It cracks under massed medium-Strength volume fire that sidesteps the wound modifier entirely, or against gunlines with enough shots to overwhelm the saves even at -1 wound.
645: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Bladeguard Veterans, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, and Sanguinary Priests providing support, this is a Liberator Assault Group list that floods the board with melee threats across multiple threat vectors — infantry on foot, jump infantry, and elite shock troops all demanding answers simultaneously. The win condition is the Liberator Assault Group's charge bonus: every charging Adeptus Astartes unit gains +2 Strength and +1 Attack on melee weapons, turning mid-tier bodies into blenders and elite units into catastrophic threats, with Lemartes pushing Death Company into overdrive and Chaplains stacking further pressure. It punishes low-model, low-armour lists that cannot absorb repeated multi-unit charges from multiple angles, quickly collapsing screening layers and taking the fight to objectives through raw combat volume. However, it struggles against gunlines with long-range anti-infantry saturation or deep-strike denial tools that prevent clean charges, since the entire damage engine requires actually connecting — forced overwatch, terrain choke, or charge-disruption mechanics peel away its teeth before the fight phase triggers.
667: Built around Lords of Change, Bloodcrushers, and Be'lakor, this list runs the Cavalcade of Chaos detachment to let its Mounted units fall back and still shoot or charge — turning every combat into a no-lose trade. The engine is relentless harassment: Bloodcrushers crash in, absorb a fight, fall back freely, then pile straight back into charges while Lords of Change and Be'lakor delete priority targets from range or melee. It punishes slow, static armies that rely on locking units in combat to neutralize threats, since the fall-back-and-charge loop completely defeats that plan. However, it struggles against high-volume anti-armour shooting or elite melee that can delete Bloodcrushers before they cycle out of danger.
666: Built around waves of Daemonettes, Fiends, Keepers of Secrets, the Contorted Epitome, a Tormentbringer, Beasts of Nurgle, and the Masque herself, this Legion of Excess force runs Warptide as its second detachment to unlock an advance-and-charge engine across the entire battleline. The plan is to flood the midtable with Daemonette hordes that advance, shoot with Assault, then immediately declare charges, while Fiends and Keepers deliver layered melee punishment across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It punishes slow, static armies that rely on holding position — the sheer volume of bodies advancing and charging every turn overloads defensive screens and makes target-priority impossible. Armies that can reliably delete entire squads at range before the charge lands, or that generate enough mortal wounds and blast weapons to carve through the horde mass, crack this list open before its momentum builds.
668: Built around Lords of Change (averaging two per list), Kairos Fateweaver, Screamers, Flamers, Pink Horrors, and Beasts of Nurgle, this Scintillating Legion force uses a deep pool of Flux tokens to re-roll critical dice across the game. The win condition is layered threat saturation — Screamers and Flamers advance into position under the Warptide strat's Assault and free-charge rules while Lords of Change and Kairos stack re-rolls through Flux to delete priority targets and deny board control. It punishes slower, static armies that can't respond to simultaneous aerial and ground threats arriving with re-roll insurance on every damaging roll. Lists that can strip key pieces early — particularly fast alpha strikers that can reach the Lords of Change before Flux tokens absorb the critical rolls — crack it open before the re-roll economy becomes overwhelming.
664: Built around Bloodcrushers, Flesh Hounds, Skullmaster, and Rendmaster on Blood Throne as a cavalry hammer core, backed by Beasts of Nurgle, Plaguebearers, Nurglings, Be'lakor, and a Bloodthirster for depth, all running Cavalcade of Chaos so every mounted unit that falls back can still shoot and charge. The plan is to crash fast-moving Khorne cavalry into the midboard, exploit the fall-back-and-charge loop to stay perpetually threatening, and layer Nurgle bodies on objectives to grind scoring through attrition. It punishes armies that rely on controlling engagement range, since the fall-back-and-charge mechanic strips away the usual reward for defensive positioning against cavalry. Dense, high-armour infantry blocks and strong melee counter-punchers can absorb the mounted wave before it generates enough kills to pull ahead on score.
665: Built around Be'lakor, a Bloodthirster, a Great Unclean One, and dense waves of Plaguebearers and Nurglings, this Shadow Legion force plays a grinding, multi-layered attrition game across every phase. Warptide lets Battleline units advance and still shoot and charge, so Plaguebearers surge into scoring positions without sacrificing combat eligibility, while Be'lakor and the Bloodthirster apply lethal pressure from deep in the opponent's half. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — the horde volume overwhelms efficient damage trades, and layered Lethal Hits across multiple combat threats make every engagement costly for fragile high-value units. However, high-volume mortal-wound output or mass blast weaponry that degrades the screen fast exposes the heavier pieces before they can meaningfully engage, and the build lacks the raw damage ceiling to reliably crack heavily armoured targets at range.
653: Built around three Defilers, nearly three Venomcrawlers, Vashtorr the Arkifane, a Warpsmith, Chaos Bikers, and Cultist screens, this is a Soulforged Warpack daemon vehicle swarm that floods the board with heavy chassis. The engine is Dark Pact abuse: Vashtorr and the Warpsmith support the vehicles' pact rolls, and once a Daemon Vehicle invokes its contract it gains +1 to wound on ranged attacks and +2 Attacks in melee, turning already-durable platforms into overloaded kill machines that score through annihilation and aggressive midboard control. It punishes elite low-model-count armies by presenting too many high-toughness threats simultaneously, overwhelming their anti-tank budget while Cultists and Bikers contest objectives. Horde lists that ignore individual vehicles and lists with reliable Dark Pact disruption or consistent mortal-wound output can crack the chassis faster than the army regenerates pressure.
647: Built around cultist mobs, traitor guardsmen, chaos bikers, defilers, chaos rhinos, and chaos predator destructors, this Pactbound Zealots list buries opponents under a tide of cheap bodies while sustaining meaningful firepower from its heavier platforms. The engine is a layered one: expendable infantry flood objectives and absorb attrition while bikers apply mobile mid-table pressure and predator destructors deliver sustained anti-armour shooting, all sharpened by Lethal Hits on melee attacks triggering on unmodified 5s. It punishes gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that struggle to clear multiple waves of screening chaff before the armoured elements grind them down. However, high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that efficiently kill horde units can collapse the screening layer and expose the mechanised core before it can dictate engagement range.
470: Built around swarms of War Dog Karnivores, War Dog Brigands, War Dog Executioners, and Cultist Mobs operating under the Houndpack Lance detachment, this list floods the table with fast, mid-sized armoured threats backed by cheap infantry chaff. The engine is the Houndpack Lance's focus mechanic — tagging a priority enemy unit each Command phase to stack Sustained Hits 1 across every War Dog attacking it, funnelling concentrated firepower and melee into sequenced kills while Cultist Mobs screen objectives and absorb punishment. It punishes armour-heavy lists brutally, layering mobile anti-tank volume from multiple angles faster than target saturation allows efficient responses. It cracks under elite infantry pressure or aggressive alpha strikes that strip the screening cultists early and expose War Dogs to being isolated and ground down before the Sustained Hits engine can cycle.
649: Built around Huron Blackheart, Abaddon the Despoiler, Chosen, Defilers, and cultist screens backed by Masters of the Maelstrom and Red Corsairs Raiders, this is a horde-brawler that floods the mid-table with durable infantry while heavy walkers and raiders provide fire support. The win condition is controlling objectives through sheer body count and then using Huron's rotating command abilities to buff whichever infantry unit needs to punch, screen, or survive that turn, creating a flexible toolkit that punishes opponents for committing to any one threat. Lists spread across multiple detachments — Murdertalon Raiders, Veterans of the Long War, Creations of Bile, and Huron's Marauders — meaning the buff package shifts list to list, but the core answer to elite, low-model-count armies is always the same: drown them in activations and score on bodies. Armies that can efficiently delete chaff at range and then isolate Huron or Abaddon away from their infantry bubble expose how dependent the list's damage output is on those characters staying alive and central.
635: Built around a squadron of Land Speeders, Land Speeder Vengeances, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Deathwing Knights, Lion El'Jonson, Azrael, Inner Circle Companions, and Scout Squads, this list runs the Darkflight Pursuit detachment to give every RAVENWING FLY unit Ignores Cover on ranged attacks. The win condition is a two-pronged kill chain: fast-moving skimmers strip armour and blast entrenched infantry with cover-negated firepower, while the Deathwing Knights and Lion push onto objectives backed by Azrael's leadership bubble. It punishes gunline armies that rely on terrain and cover saves to survive, because the Ignores Cover rule turns defensive positioning into a wasted investment. Where it cracks is against aggressive melee threats that can tie up or kill the speeders early, collapsing the ranged engine before the knights can answer.
652: Built around Defilers, Cultist Mobs, Chaos Bikers, Abaddon the Despoiler, Nurglings, and Vashtorr the Arkifane, this Pactbound Zealots list combines daemon engine firepower with a layered melee and screening package — Lethal Hits on unmodified 5s in melee applies across the entire roster, making every combat punch harder than the statline suggests. The plan is to grind the mid-table with Bikers and Defilers cracking armour while Cultists and Nurglings contest and deny, letting Abaddon and Vashtorr clean up whatever survives into a killable position. It punishes armour-heavy gunlines that expect to out-range it, using mobile anti-armour threats from multiple vectors to overload target priority. Concentrated elite melee or fast alpha-strike lists can strip its mid-board presence before the Lethal Hits engine engages, and its diffuse, mid-cost unit spread offers no single answer to high-volume anti-infantry pressure.
638: Built around Ravenwing Black Knights, Ravenwing Command Squad, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and Azrael — with Lion El'Jonson anchoring nearly three lists in five — this is a dual-wing hammer that pairs fast-moving bike units with heavily armoured terminator elites to contest across the entire board simultaneously. The plan is to use the Ravenwing's mobility to apply early pressure and lock opponents in engagement range while the Deathwing Knights and Inner Circle Companions crash into midfield to grind out kills and hold primary objectives through sheer durability. It punishes elite-light gunlines that lack the volume of attacks needed to chew through terminator saves and high-toughness bikers before the engagement starts tilting on points. High-damage alpha strikes and strong anti-vehicle overload crack it open, since losing expensive elite pieces early collapses the threat saturation the list depends on.
640: Built around Azrael, multiple Librarians (including Terminator-armoured), Inner Circle Companions, and Deathwing Knights screened by Intercessors and Scouts, this is a psychic-buffed melee-and-fire hybrid list operating under the Inner Circle Task Force and Librarius Conclave detachments. The core engine is using Vowed objective markers to anchor scoring while Librarius Conclave disciplines — most often Divination's hit-and-wound re-rolls or Biomancy's movement boost — fuel a grinding advance that drops Deathwing Knights and Companions into key zones. It punishes lists that rely on mid-board infantry engagements, where layered psychic buffs and Terminator durability simply outattrition opponents fighting for the same ground. It cracks against elite anti-armour shooting and alpha-strike lists that can strip Terminators before the Vowed objective engine gets traction.
451: Built around Drazhar, Archons, Incubi, Wyches, and Kabalite Warriors packed into Venoms and Raiders, this is a fast-moving transport swarm that combines Kabalite Agonysts' Sustained Hits 1 on ranged attacks with Skysplinter Assault's post-disembark Lance melee and Ignores Cover shooting to deliver layered punishment the moment anything unloads. The plan is to flood the board with cheap bodies holding objectives while elite combat units — Drazhar and Incubi chief among them — disembark with Lance weapons to crack saves that would otherwise hold, backed by Ravagers and Scourges providing mobile anti-armour from range. It punishes infantry-heavy lists brutally, drowning them under Sustained Hits volleys and multi-unit melee pile-ins that horde armies simply cannot absorb. What cracks it open is high-volume, high-AP shooting that kills transports before they unload — stranding fragile infantry in the open and collapsing the entire delivery engine in one shooting phase.
596: Built around Librarians (both on foot and in Terminator armour), Deathwatch Veterans, Indomitor Kill Teams, Deathwatch Terminator Squads, and Sternguard Veterans operating under the Bastion Task Force and Librarius Conclave detachments, this is a heavy gunline that floods the board with elite infantry crammed into transports. The engine is Bastion Task Force's Battleline rule — Intercessors and other Battleline units shoot and perform Actions after Advancing or Falling Back, keeping the scoring machine running while the Librarius Conclave cycles psychic disciplines (Divination's re-rolls for volume shooting, Biomancy for repositioning) to maximize firepower from stationary kill teams and Veterans. It punishes static elite armies that can't threaten the transport bubble, overwhelming them with layered small-arms and special weapons before they close distance.
