Armies that can strip transports early or apply volume mortal-wound pressure crack it open, since the infantry inside loses both its mobility and its action-economy engine simultaneously.
654: Built around Archon, Lady Malys, Drazhar, Lelith Hesperax, Incubi, Wyches, and Scourges riding a fleet of Venoms and Raiders, this is a mass-skimmer list blending Exhibition Of Slaughter's Lethal Hits on Wych Cult melee attacks with Skysplinter Assault's disembark-triggered Ignores Cover on ranged weapons and Lance on melee weapons. The win condition is coordinated burst turns: units pile out of transports to strip saves with Lance melee and punch through light cover with Ignores Cover shooting, while Scourges with heavy weapons provide sustained fire pressure across the board. It punishes mid-density infantry armies that lack the volume to screen every transport lane, as layered Lethal Hits and Lance stack devastatingly against multi-wound non-vehicle targets. It cracks open against alpha-strike lists that can delete transports before disembarkation, collapsing the entire combo chain before it fires.
672: Built around Infractors, Tormentors, Lord Exultants, Defilers, Chaos Rhinos, Daemonic Princes with Wings, Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, Lucius the Eternal, and Chaos Spawn, this list plays a pledge-driven kill engine inside the Coterie of the Conceited, using Rhino-mounted infantry to threaten objectives while mobile anti-armour elements hunt targets to meet each round's Pact point quota. The win condition is calibrating your pledge carefully each battle round — commit to a realistic kill count, bank Pact points consistently, and snowball those resources while Defilers and Winged Princes crack armour and Infractors contest aggressively from transports. It punishes midfield brawler armies that hand over bunched, killable units, making pledge thresholds easy to hit while denying the opponent safe positioning. Lists that screen tightly, deny clean charges, and force you to overcommit on pledges unravel the engine — miss your number and you bank nothing, stalling the Pact point economy entirely.
675: Built around Chaos Spawn, Infractors, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Defilers, Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, and Lucius the Eternal, all ferried forward in Rhinos with a winged Daemon Prince providing mobile threat, this is a mid-table brawler that floods objectives with cheap, durable chaff while elite melee infantry do the killing. The core engine is Infractors and Tormentors piling out of transports to contest and fight, with Spawn soaking return fire and Lords Exultant amplifying nearby units into dangerous combat threats. It punishes infantry-heavy armies that can't clear durable chaff efficiently, letting Spawn screen key pieces while Flawless Blades and Noise Marines grind through lighter targets. Armies that pack high-volume anti-armour or elite melee that ignores its screening layer can crack the transport bubble early and strand key units before they reach engagement range.
633: Built around Achilles Ridgerunners, Purestrain Genestealers, Neophyte Hybrids, Hyperadapted Raveners, Patriarch, Deathleaper, Benefictus, Acolyte Hybrids, Lictors, Atalan Jackals, and Reductus Saboteurs, this Final Day list blends native Genestealer Cult horde bodies with a massive Tyranid Vanguard Invader allotment — nearly every slot available at Strike Force. The plan is to flood every lane simultaneously, using mid-table brawlers like Raveners and Purestrains to threaten fights while Ridgerunners and Jackals apply mobile pressure and contest secondaries from range. Neophyte Hybrids healing inside terrain and Purestrain cycling via strategic reserves through Purestrain Broodswarm give the list exceptional attrition depth, punishing armies that can't sustain kill output across multiple turns. The sheer unit diversity and mixed keyword pool means it frays badly against hard alpha strikes and elite shooting that can delete key pieces before the layered threat web locks in.
688: Built around Nemesis Dreadknights, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, and Interceptor Squads screened by Strike Squads, this is a mobile hammer list that floods the board with heavy walkers and teleporting infantry across a detachment-agnostic framework of Immaterial Interdiction and Sanctic Spearhead. The plan is to leverage Sanctic Spearhead's 6" Advance bonus and Assault conversion on Grey Knights Vehicles to drive Dreadknights into mid-board early, then use Interceptor surge moves to threaten objectives and force unfavorable trades while the Grand Masters amplify the kill chain. It punishes slower armoured lists that cannot contest mid-board efficiently, as multiple high-damage walkers advancing at threat ranges most opponents aren't built to handle across the whole table. However, mass high-volume shooting or deep-strike denial armies that can isolate and focus individual Dreadknights before they consolidate will crack the list open, since losing even one walker early collapses the damage math significantly.
634: Built around Atalan Jackals, Achilles Ridgerunners, Goliath Rockgrinders, Acolyte Hybrids with hand flamers, Purestrain Genestealers, Reductus Saboteurs, Neophyte Hybrids, and a Patriarch, this is a dense mechanised horde running the Outlander Claw detachment with frequent support from Purestrain Broodswarm and Xenocult Masses. The plan is to use Jackals' sticky-objective ability to lock down controlled markers early while Rockgrinders and Ridgerunners apply mobile anti-armour pressure and hand-flamer Acolytes erase screens in melee, generating a sustained scoring lead that opponents can never fully claw back. It punishes elite low-model armies by flooding the board with layered threats across every phase — vehicles with boosted OC, cheap chaff soaking return fire, and Purestrains cycling back through strategic reserves. However, high-volume mortal-wound output and alpha-strike lists that can collapse the vehicle core before the sticky control engine activates will leave the Jackals holding objectives with no protective umbrella.
689: Built around Grand Master Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Castellan Crowe with Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this Brotherhood Strike list drops hard from deep strike and floods objectives with durable infantry. The engine is a deep-strike alpha: units arriving from reserve gain re-rolls to hit and wound of 1 on that turn, while Purgation Squads pin targets and force battle-shock rolls at -1, stacking pressure to strip leadership and punish battered units. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't screen every deep strike vector, overwhelming them with simultaneous multi-angle threats before they stabilize. It cracks against dense screen armies that wall off deep strike lanes and durable hordes that shrug off the turn-one burst and grind back through its mid-tier staying power.
615: Built around Berehk Stornbröw, Einhyr Hearthguard, Cthonian Beserks, and Kâhls backed by Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Sagitaurs, and Hekaton Land Fortresses, this list plays Hearthguard Covenant and floods the midboard with durable, high-output infantry supported by heavy armour. The engine is close-range annihilation: Hearthguard Covenant's wound-roll re-rolls within 9" amplify both the Hearthguard and Kâhls into elite-erasing kill machines, while Cthonian Beserks pressure screens and contest objectives, generating YP to fuel secondary oathband abilities. It punishes elite infantry-heavy and low-model-count armies brutally, drowning them in wound re-rolls and melee threat across multiple vectors simultaneously. Horde lists and armies with strong long-range anti-tank can stretch it thin by forcing difficult target-priority decisions before it closes the 9" window.
700: Built around Cerastus Knight Lancers and Canis Rex, this is an aggressively mobile Imperial Knights list running the Questoris Companions detachment, which rewards you for completing Oaths by generating additional ones each turn, creating a compounding engine of bonuses as the game progresses. The plan is to leverage elite mobility and heavy anti-armour output to threaten the entire board early, banking Oath completions to snowball combat effectiveness while giant chassis lock down key objectives by sheer physical presence. It punishes slow, static, or vehicle-heavy lists that can't reliably threaten multiple large Knights simultaneously, as spreading anti-tank fire thin rarely kills anything before it scores. The weakness is elite infantry or high-volume mortal-wound output that can chip wounds faster than the Oath engine generates value, and anything that can screen out the Lancers' charge angles collapses the aggressive tempo the list depends on.
621: Built around multiple Hekaton Land Fortresses supported by Einhyr Hearthguard, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Ironkin Steeljacks with heavy volkanite disintegrators, and Ûthar the Destined, this list plants a dense firebase midboard and dares opponents to walk into it. The win condition is volume-of-fire attrition: Sagitaurs and Kapricus Carriers push infantry into threat range while Hearthguard re-roll wound rolls of 1 against anything within 9", and Thunderkyn alongside the Steeljacks provide layered anti-armour and anti-infantry overload. It punishes slow, durable armies that have to advance into the killzone, where stacked re-rolls and sustained hits grind through high-toughness units efficiently. It cracks against mobile alpha-strike lists that can threaten the Hekatons early, strip the firebase's coherence before it gets established, and score secondaries around the stationary castle's flanks.
617: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carriers, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, this is a mid-board brawler that layers fast skimmer harassment over a heavy gunline core, all running under the Farseekers detachment granting +1 to hit for Hernkyn units within 12". The plan is to push Pioneers and Yaegirs aggressively into the mid-table, generate YP through kills or Hostile Acquisition, and spend that currency to keep the army's abilities cycling while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses grind down anything that answers back. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that cannot contest the mid-board early, as the close-range +1 to hit bonus makes concentrated Pioneer volleys disproportionately efficient against tough targets. However, alpha-strike lists that can strip the exposed skimmer screen before YP accrues, or highly mobile armies that deny the 12" engagement bubble entirely, leave the gunline core isolated and unable to convert its firepower into board control.
620: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Kapricus Carriers, and Hekaton Land Fortresses, with Memnyr Strategists, Einhyr Hearthguard, Hearthkyn Warriors, Ûthar the Destined, and Sagitaurs rounding out a dense midfield presence — this is a Farseekers list that weaponises the detachment's +1 to hit for Hernkyn units within 12" to turn a swarming scout screen into a precision kill engine. The plan is to flood the midboard with cheap, mobile Hernkyn units, stack two-thirds of lists' Needgaârd Oathband YP generation from destroyed enemy units, and feed that economy into sustained pressure that scores through attrition rather than corner-camping. It punishes horde and mid-density infantry lists hard, where the combination of high model counts, transport-delivered Hearthguard, and point-blank Thunderkyn volleys generates reliable destroy triggers. Concentrated high-damage alpha strikes or elite armour that parks outside the 12" Hernkyn bubble can strip the accuracy advantage and outpace the YP engine before it snowballs.
619: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard and Kâhl delivering AP-improved melee strikes through Hearthband's core rule, backed by Hekaton Land Fortresses, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Sagitaurs laying down a punishing gunline, this list blends armoured transports with deep elite infantry to contest every table quarter simultaneously. The win condition is grinding attrition through the mid-board: Hearthguard punch into the closest eligible threat with wound re-rolls and sharpened AP while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses erase anything they can't reach, converting board control into primary points. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb both the shooting output and the subsequent melee counter-charge, especially anything that relies on 2+ armour saves. Armies that can screen the mid-board cheaply, deny Hearthguard their preferred engagement range, or outrange the gunline with long-ranged high-volume fire will force the list into awkward positions it can't melee its way out of.
616: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhl leaders, Cthonian Beserks, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, this Hearthband list is a grinding mid-table brawler that pairs heavy melee pressure with a solid firebase. The Hearthband detachment's core interaction drives everything: Hearthguard and Kâhls hit the closest eligible target to gain AP improvement on top of re-rolling wound 1s, so the plan is to close distance fast — with Beserks and Hearthguard threatening melee engagements — while Thunderkyn and Sagitaurs hammer anything that holds back. Hernkyn Pioneers and Yaegirs provide cheap screening and objective reach, letting the heavy hitters punch forward without bleeding secondary points. It punishes armies with mid-tier armour saves that can't kite reliably, but struggles against anything fast enough to deny the AP-bonus proximity trigger or durable enough to weather the storm from range before the melee wave arrives.
618: Built around Sagitaurs (Scouts 6" from Armoured Trailblazers), Cthonian Beserks, Kapricus Carriers, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and a dense infantry core of Hearthkyn Warriors, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Hernkyn Pioneers, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Ironkin Steeljacks, this is an aggressive mechanised brawler that puts armoured bodies on objectives before the opponent can react. The plan is to Scout up the Sagitaurs to threaten early pressure, deliver Beserks into combat through transport or deep strike (via Dêlve Assault Shift in a third of lists), and grind the mid-board through sheer volume of transported infantry while Thunderkyn and Steeljacks handle heavy targets. It punishes slower gunlines that lack the volume or positioning to contest multiple armoured threats simultaneously across the mid-table. It struggles against fast, high-AP alpha-strike lists that can crack transports early and strip the infantry before they can brawl.
455: Built around Nekrosor Ammentar, Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Destroyers, their respective Lords, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, the Void Dragon, and Lychguard, this is a Cursed Legion list that weaponizes the detachment's Strength bonus — starting at +2 and climbing higher once a Destroyer Cult unit kills or cripples something — to turn every Destroyer unit into a threat that punches well above its points cost. The win condition is a cascading kill chain: get one Destroyer unit to cross the destruction threshold early, trigger the escalating Strength buff, then let the rest of the Destroyer swarm tear through progressively harder targets while holding midboard objectives with Lychguard and the Void Dragon. It brutally punishes armies that present mid-toughness, multi-wound elite infantry — the kind of targets where the stacked Strength bonuses hit breakpoints and delete units wholesale, snowballing the buff again. However, it cracks open against armies that deny the first kill or dilute the board with disposable screening chaff, preventing the cascade from ever starting.
659:
Built around the Void Dragon, Nightbringer, Deceiver, one or more Transcendent C'tan, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list fields an overwhelming mass of individually powerful god-monsters and deep-striking melee threats with no single anchor that defines its identity across all lists.

The win condition is elite-unit removal and objective denial by simultaneous pressure — multiple C'tan hit different table quadrants while Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers deep strike directly onto contested objectives, forcing opponents to split answers they rarely have in sufficient volume.

It punishes lists that rely on a single elite damage dealer or centralized screen, since the sheer number of independent C'tan threats guarantees at least two or three engagements the opponent simply cannot adequately answer in the same turn.

Its critical vulnerability is high-volume, point-efficient anti-tank firepower spread across the army: losing one C'tan is survivable, but concentrated shooting that degrades two or three simultaneously collapses the pressure engine before the melee threats can close distance.
658: Built around the Void Dragon, the Nightbringer, Ophydian Destroyers, and Imotekh the Stormlord, this list runs multiple C'tan Shards under the Pantheon of Woe detachment, whose Distortion Fields aura shreds enemy armour saves by improving AP by 1 on all attacks targeting units within 6" of any Necrons Monster. The plan is to push C'tan aggressively into the midboard, overlapping their auras to stack AP degradation, then use Ophydian Destroyers to strike out of deep strike and pick apart anything already softened by the field. It punishes armies relying on invulnerable-save-free high-armour units by stripping saves through AP manipulation rather than raw damage volume. However, lists that answer with mass mortal wounds, high-AP shooting, or simply outrange the 6" aura bubble before the C'tan close can kite the slow Monster anchors and dismantle the scoring engine before it engages.
603: Built around Tankbustas, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Big Mek Dakkariggs, Flash Gitz, and Gretchin screens rolling under the More Dakka! detachment, this is a midboard gunline that floods the table with cheap bodies and packs serious anti-armour punch. The plan is to advance infantry freely via the Assault keyword on all ranged attacks, park Tankbustas and Flash Gitz in scoring positions, then detonate the Waaagh! to layer Sustained Hits 1 on top and delete priority targets through sheer volume of fire. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot clear a mass horde screen before the guns behind it open up. It struggles against fast aggressive lists that can crash into the midboard early, disrupting positioning before the Waaagh! comes online.
702: Built around Gretchin screens, Boyz, Nobz, and Bannernobs flooding the midboard, with Ghazghkull Thraka and Warbosses driving a core of Trukks and Battlewagons, all running Freebooter Krew. The plan is to designate a loot objective each Command phase and overwhelm it with a wall of bodies while Sustained Hits 1 on every Infantry, Mounted, and Walker attack — triggered when a unit is near the loot objective — pumps Flash Gitz and Boyz into lethal volume fire. Kommandos add a flanking threat that forces opponents to split attention, and the sheer model count punishes elite low-body armies that can't clear objectives fast enough under attrition. Horde-hate lists with massed high-AP blasts or combat-focused alpha-strike armies can gut the screen before the loot-objective engine gets rolling.
677: Built around multiple Librarians buffing Intercessors, Scout Squads, and Bladeguard Veterans, this list floods mid-table with durable infantry bodies screened by cheap scouts while psyker-fuelled disciplines rotate between movement, accuracy, and firepower depending on the matchup. The win condition is objective saturation through volume — layered infantry screens hold secondaries while Bladeguard punch forward to lock enemy scoring units in melee and Librarian buffs convert mid-strength firepower into meaningful damage trades. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear numerous tough infantry blobs, particularly when Divination Discipline turns mass bolt fire into a reliable grind. However, it cracks under high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that make the infantry density a liability rather than a strength.
678: Built around Captain Titus, Marneus Calgar, Bladeguard Veterans, Wardens of Ultramar, Terminator Assault Squads, and Ballistus Dreadnoughts under the Librarius Conclave with Reclamation Force, this list marries a durable melee core to a heavy gunline superstructure. The engine is Reclamation Force's dual payoff — AP improvement on melee attacks onto contested objectives punishes anything trying to trade on points, while the defensive buff on controlled markers keeps anchoring units alive through return fire. Scouts and Intercessors spread thin across the board to lock objective control early, letting the elite melee hammer of Titus, Calgar, and Bladeguard crash into whatever threatens the scoring zones. It struggles against armies that can strip the objective screen with mass low-AP shooting before the melee wave arrives, leaving the AP bonus without a target and the defensive shield with nothing to protect.
686: Built around Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and a screen of Scout and Intercessor squads, this is a mobile anti-armour gunline that deploys its entire Speeder contingent via ingress moves at the top of Turn 1. The win condition is overwhelming armour-kill at range — Hammerstrikes and Thunderstrikes reposition freely while infantry hold objectives and absorb pressure, generating score through primary control and secondary picks enabled by that map-wide mobility. It punishes armour-heavy and vehicle-dense lists badly, concentrating anti-tank volume that most mechanised armies cannot survive while maintaining enough boots on the ground to contest the mid-table. Armies that can crack light infantry cheaply — clearing the Scout and Intercessor screen — and then tie up the Speeders in close combat or deny their angles with dense terrain exposure will expose how fragile this build's objective-holders truly are.
681:
Built around Librarians in Terminator Armour, Terminator Assault Squads, Bladeguard Veterans, and Marneus Calgar, this list runs the Librarius Conclave with Reclamation Force as a secondary detachment, flexing between Psychic Disciplines each battle round to suit the moment — Divination for reliable output, Biomancy for extra reach, Pyromancy for board pressure.

The engine is melee objective control: Reclamation Force's AP improvement on objective-marker attacks turns already-dangerous Terminators and Bladeguard into objective-erasing hammers, while Calgar amplifies nearby units and Scouts provide cheap early board presence and screening.

It punishes mid-tier melee armies that lack the volume to trade efficiently, as the AP bonus and Calgar's support make objective fights deeply lopsided against anything short of elite defensive lines.

However, it struggles against high-volume shooting or dedicated anti-heavy firepower that can strip Terminators before they reach objectives, cracking open a list with no robust ranged answer and slow-moving core units.
679: Built around Marneus Calgar, Cato Sicarius, Victrix Honour Guard, Scout Squads, Incursor Squads, Intercessors, Repulsor Executioners, and Ballistus Dreadnoughts operating under the Ceramite Sentinels detachment, this list plants itself into terrain and fights from fortified positions — every unit garrisoned inside a feature re-rolls hit and wound rolls of 1, and qualifies for the Entrenched keyword if it didn't arrive that turn. The plan is to hold terrain features across the board with durable infantry screens while Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts pour sustained firepower downrange, using Calgar and Sicarius to keep key units fighting above their weight. It punishes slow, short-ranged armies that must walk into the killzone, and bleeds opponents who cannot efficiently clear entrenched infantry off objectives turn after turn. However, fast alpha-strike lists that flood the board on turn one deny the Entrenched keyword entirely, stripping the detachment's core defensive benefit before it ever pays off.
695: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators in multiple squads, Logan Grimnar, Ragnar Blackmane, Arjac Rockfist, the Wolf Guard Headtakers, Blood Claws, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, and a Wolf Guard Battle Leader, this is a melee-heavy character-and-elite swarm running Saga of the Great Wolf — cycling its Hunting Packs each Command phase to layer re-rolls and offensive buffs across the entire force. The plan is to flood mid-table with durable, character-supported melee threats, forcing the opponent to answer multiple dangerous units simultaneously while Intercessors hold home objectives and the big names punch through priority targets. It punishes slower gunlines that can't kill enough threats per turn, overwhelming them through sheer volume of hard-hitting units arriving behind Blood Claw and Terminator pressure. Armies with strong screening, reliable mortal wound output, or elite melee of their own can isolate and delete the character anchors before the Hunting Pack synergies come online.
680: Built around Caanok Var, Terminator Assault Squads, and a supporting core of Terminators in armour, Librarians in Terminator armour, Scouts, and the Ancient in Terminator armour, this Hammer of Avernii list combines a persistent Oath of Moment engine with massed Terminator melee to grind through the enemy line. The core plan is to keep Caanok Var alive and cycling Oath of Moment targets via RECALCULATING, ensuring re-roll-wounds-of-1 never goes offline while Assault Terminators repeatedly crash into priority threats. It punishes mid-table brawler armies that want to trade melee, as layered wound re-rolls and the Ancient's support stack make each Terminator brick hit above its weight. It cracks under elite shooting that can delete Caanok Var early, collapsing the target-cycling engine and leaving the Assault Terminators without reliable wound support.
676: Built around Infernus Squads, Eradicators, and Librarians riding in a Land Raider Redeemer, with Vulkan He'stan and Adrax Agatone as fire-support warlords, this list weaponizes the Firestorm Assault Force's core rule: every ranged weapon gains Assault, and attacks within 12" hit at +1 Strength, turning short-range shooting into a wall of supercharged firepower. It cracks open against elite armies that can screen the 12" kill-zone or outrange it entirely, denying the Strength bonus and forcing the gunline to shoot at base profile.
682: Built around Darnath Lysander, Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, Vanguard Veterans with jump packs, Bladeguard Veterans, and a Librarian, this is a dense, multi-wave melee and fire-support list running the Emperor's Shield detachment, which hands Lysander full wound re-rolls against the Oath of Moment target and gives the broader army wound-1 re-rolls on the same target. 528: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, and Grey Hunters flooding the board in volume, this is a Saga of the Great Wolf list that cycles its Hunting Pack selections each Command phase to layer re-rolls, buffs, and pressure across an entire wave of Adeptus Astartes units simultaneously. 614: Built around Commander Farsight, multiple Crisis Battlesuit teams (Starscythe, Fireknife, and Sunforge loadouts), Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinders, Broadsides, Ghostkeels, and the Twin Lance, this is an aggressive close-range battlesuit swarm running Retaliation Cadre — which boosts Strength on all battlesuit ranged attacks within 12" and further improves AP inside 8". 599: Built around Neurolictor, Lictor, Genestealer, Broodlord, Von Ryan's Leapers, Hyperadapted Raveners, and Raveners, with Biovores and Deathleaper rounding out a swarm of fast, infiltrating killers, this list runs the Ambush Predators detachment to give its Lictor and Neurolictor deep strike and character-hunting re-rolls. 612: Built around Slaughterbound, Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, Daemon Prince of Khorne, and Jakhals screening, this is a relentless melee swarm running the Possessed Slaughterband detachment, where every shot the opponent takes risks triggering Brazen Fury surge moves that close distance and disrupt gunlines before they can finish their work. 708: Built around Allarus Custodians, Caladius Grav-Tanks, Witchseekers, Custodian Guard, a Blade Champion, and a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, this list splits between Tharanatoi Hammerblow's ingress-then-charge threat with Terminators and Solar Spearhead's vehicle OC-boosting presence. 439: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, massed Skitarii Marshals, Tech-Priest Manipuli, Hastarii Fusiliers, Rangers, Vanguard, Sicarian Infiltrators, and Servitor Battleclades delivered aboard Skorpius Duneriders, with Ironstrider Ballistarii providing mobile anti-armour support. 741: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Kasrkin, Gaunt's Ghosts, Ursula Creed, Scout Sentinels, Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, and Krieg Combat Engineers, this is a dense infantry gunline that deep strikes elite kill units while flooding the board with expendable bodies. 586: Built around waves of Daemonettes, Fiends, Beasts of Nurgle, Keepers of Secrets, the Contorted Epitome, the Tormentbringer, and the Masque of Slaanesh, this list weaponises both Legion Of Excess and Warptide to create a perpetual-motion assault engine: Daemonettes advance and still charge, Fell Back units re-engage the same turn, and nothing ever truly disengages. 747: Built around War Dog Stalkers, Karnivores, and Brigands — six to eight fast, aggressive light Knights swarming the board with overlapping threat vectors. 729: Built around Chaos Bikers, Cultist Mobs, Traitor Guardsmen, Defilers, and Chaos Rhinos operating under Pactbound Zealots, this list floods the board with cheap bodies while parking Daemon Engine firepower at range. It cracks when opponents bring truly high-Strength or high-volume firepower that bypasses the resilience bonus entirely, exposing how point-heavy and relatively low-model-count the roster really is.
636: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and Hellblasters led by Azrael, with Inner Circle Companions and Scout Squads providing bodies, this list leans heavily on Dark Age Arsenal's +1 Strength to plasma across every profile. It punishes mechanised and multi-wound infantry lists hard, where stacked plasma volume and mobile anti-armour overload damage-mitigation saves. Anything that can close fast and tie up the speeders in melee, or force the list into bad terrain where board presence collapses, will crack it open.

628: Built around Poxwalkers, Plague Marines, Deathshroud Terminators, Malignant Plaguecasters, the Lord of Contagion, Typhus, the Biologus Putrifier, the Tallyman, Myphitic Blight-Haulers, and Chaos Spawn, this list runs Champions Of Contagion to hot-swap its active Plague each battle round, with most lists also stacking Paragons Of Putrescence to push Character Contagion Range out to 12", blanketing the mid-board in overlapping debuff auras. 701: Built around Deathwatch Veterans, Deathwatch Terminators, dual Librarians, and Intercessor squads, this is a mid-table shooting and brawling force that leans on Firestorm Assault Force in most lists to give its ranged weapons Assault and a Strength bump inside 12", turning aggressive repositioning into raw killing power. 744: Built around Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, Maulerfiends, Defilers, Lords Exultant, Infractors in Rhinos, Tormentors, Noise Marines, and Flawless Blades, this Coterie of the Conceited list drives a wall of mobile threat into the mid-board every turn. 746: Built around Chaos Rhinos ferrying Infractors, Tormentors, and Noise Marines into position, supported by Lords Exultant, Daemon Princes with wings, Flawless Blades, Defilers, and walls of Chaos Spawn absorbing punishment at the front. It punishes slower combat armies and horde infantry that can't survive Fights First pressure backed by high-volume melee output. It struggles against gunlines and alpha-strike lists that strip the Rhino transports before the charge lands, leaving the melee core exposed and reactive.

754: Built around Nemesis Dreadknights, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Interceptor Squads, and Strike Squads, this list runs Sanctic Spearhead to slam its Dreadknights up the board with a flat 6" Advance bonus and full Assault firepower on the move, keeping pressure constant from turn one. 753: Built around Castellan Crowe, multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this Warpbane Task Force list uses Purifier positioning to physically extend Hallowed Ground across the midboard, layering objective control with a mobile elite infantry core. It punishes slow or static armies that cannot contest multiple midfield objectives simultaneously, as the combined threat range of Dreadknights and Terminators forces an opponent to defend everywhere at once. Highly mobile elite forces that can collapse individual Purifier squads — breaking Hallowed Ground coverage — and armies with sufficient long-range firepower to strip Dreadknights before they engage will crack this list open.
740: Built around Watch Masters leading Deathwatch Kill Teams, Imperial Navy Breachers, Subductor Squads, and a supporting cast of Inquisitors Draxus and Kroyle, a Navigator, a Rogue Trader Entourage, a Culexus Assassin, and Imperial Rhinos pushing infantry forward under Imperialis Fleet. 756: Built around multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Purifier Squads, and Castellan Crowe, this list runs either Fires of Purgation or Warpbane Task Force to layer psychic shooting pressure across the board. It punishes horde-heavy armies hardest, where massed psychic firepower and battle-shock cascades can strip bodies and deny actions simultaneously. It cracks open against elite low-model-count armies that shrug off battle-shock and can surgically remove Purgation Squads before the pinning engine comes online.
761: Built around Armiger Helverins, Armiger Warglaives, and Knight Crusaders, this list pairs the Throne-Bonded Outriders detachment's Bondsman-triggered Ignores Cover on Armigers with the Valourstrike Lance's Advance-and-fire Assault rule, keeping the entire force mobile without sacrificing firepower. 522: Built around multiple squads of Cthonian Beserks deep striking across the board, supported by Berehk Stornbröw, the Memnyr Strategist, Einhyr Hearthguard in Kapricus Carriers, and Hekaton Land Fortresses providing heavy fire from range, this list uses the Dêlve Assault Shift detachment to threaten every midfield objective simultaneously. Aggressive anti-horde shooting or armies that can screen the full midfield early will collapse the timing window the Beserks need, leaving this list overextended and under-scoring.
579: Built around Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, Skorpekh Lords and Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, Hexmark Destroyers, Imotekh, Canoptek Reanimators, and Technomancers operating under Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit for CHARACTER-led units, this is a highly mobile toolbox army that floods the board with fast, resilient threats across every phase. However, high-volume mortal wound output or elite melee that bypasses reanimation can dismantle the layered durability, and a true alpha strike that removes the CHARACTER leaders collapses the hit-bonus engine before it fires.
739: Built around Skorpekh Lords leading Skorpekh Destroyers and Ophydian Destroyers, supported by Canoptek Wraiths, C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, and a deep resurrection engine of Technomancers, Canoptek Reanimators, and Nekrosor Ammentar, this Awakened Dynasty list hits with melee aggression while constantly recycling bodies. Where it cracks is against mass mortal wounds or volume attacks that overwhelm the reanimation math before it can proc, particularly from gunlines that can spread damage across multiple units faster than Technomancers can patch them.
767: Built around Boyz in volume, Painboyz keeping them alive, Ghazghkull Thraka and the Warboss hammering the midfield, Gretchin screening objectives, and Kommandos threatening flanks via Scouts 6" from Equatorial Hordes, this list runs the dual-detachment engine of Equatorial Hordes and Freebooter Krew to flood the board with bodies and contest on all fronts. The win condition is simple brutality: Freebooter Krew's loot objective focuses scoring pressure each turn while Sustained Hits 1 from Freebooter Krew turns every Ork Infantry attack into a volume-of-hits machine, letting the Boyz and Flash Gitz grind through almost anything in the midfield brawl. It punishes low-model-count elite armies by overwhelming them with wound output and attrition, with Painboyz sustaining the frontline long enough to make trading deeply unfavorable for the opponent. Single-model or small-unit alpha strike lists that can delete key characters like Ghazghkull before the charge land are the real threat, since losing the beatstick anchor collapses the close-combat pressure the whole plan depends on.
557: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Beastboss characters, Squighog Boyz, Boyz, Gretchin screens, Kill Rig, Ghazghkull Thraka, Mozrog Skragbad, Painboy support, and Kommandos, this is a thundering green tide that floods the midboard with expendable bodies and hard-hitting Beast Snagga units. The plan is to plant multiple massive infantry blobs on objectives while Squighog Boyz and Ghazghkull punch through whatever is holding them, generating pressure across every lane simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model armies badly — those opponents simply cannot kill enough models fast enough to deny board control before the Orks crush them in melee. Tightly packed, high-damage shooting armies that can thin the horde before contact, combined with anti-horde area denial, are the primary threat, as losing model count early collapses the combat weight the list depends on.
683: Built around Librarians, Heavy Intercessors, Intercessors, Assault Intercessors, and an Apothecary Biologis, this is a dense infantry wall powered by the Bastion Task Force detachment, which lets Adeptus Astartes Battleline units shoot, charge, and perform Actions after Advancing or Falling Back. The engine is sustained board control: Battleline units stay on objectives while still contributing firepower and applying a debuff to hit enemy units after resolving attacks, letting the Apothecary Biologis keep squads topped up and the Librarius Conclave's rotating Psychic Disciplines layer on re-rolls or mobility as needed. It punishes elite, low-model armies that can't clear volume — the sheer number of Battleline bodies, backed by healing, overwhelms precision removal tools. It cracks under massed high-AP shooting or deep-strike alpha strikes that bypass the screen and delete key healing pieces before they can stabilise the blob.
554: Built around Aethon Shaan, Kayvaan Shrike, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Inceptors, Vanguard Veterans with Jump Packs, Scouts, Incursors, Infiltrators, and Centurion Devastators, this Shadowmark Talon list marries a persistent ranged defence — every unit outside 12" benefits from cover — with a mobile jump-pack assault core that threatens the whole board. The engine is Aethon's Unparalleled Tactician ability, which feeds free Into Darkness Stratagem uses to keep the jump infantry surging forward unpredictably while Centurion Devastators anchor the backfield with heavy fire. It punishes slower gunlines that struggle to close within 12", where the cover bonus evaporates and the jump units are already among their targets. Tight, fast melee armies that can collapse the engagement range immediately, denying the cover window and hitting the relatively fragile infantry before they can reposition, crack it open.
760: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Terminator Assault Squad, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, and Arjac Rockfist, this is a transport-heavy terminator hammer that floods the mid-table with armoured bodies. 759: Built around Logan Grimnar, multiple squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, a Captain in Terminator Armour, and a Land Raider Redeemer, this is a Saga of the Great Wolf elite-terminator hammer that floods the mid-table with armoured bodies. It punishes lighter elite armies that lack the volume of attacks to chew through multiple Terminator squads before being overwhelmed in the mid-board brawl. It cracks when faced with high-AP, high-volume shooting that can strip Terminators faster than the army can close distance or re-screen.
773: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Rubric Marines, and supporting Sorcerers, this is a transport-heavy infantry phalanx that floods mid-board with bodies while maintaining a layered psychic support structure across multiple detachment configurations. It excels against elite low-model-count armies that struggle to generate enough attacks to chew through stacked invulnerable saves and the Rubricae's built-in damage-1 armour save bonus simultaneously. It cracks open under sustained high-damage, multi-vector pressure — anything that bypasses invulnerables with mortal wounds or spikes consistent Damage 2+ attacks can outpace the healing engine before it stabilises.
771: Built around Sorcerers in Terminator Armour leading Scarab Occult Terminators, supported by Sekhetar Robots, Rubric Marines, Tzaangors, and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, this list plays a layered, mass-horde castle that floods the board with durable Psychic units across multiple tiers of toughness. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot clear multiple durable screening layers fast enough, trading efficiently across all phases. Mortal-wound spam and high-volume anti-horde shooting crack it open by bypassing invulnerable saves and thinning the screens that protect the expensive Terminator anchor.
772: Built around Magnus the Red, a winged Daemon Prince, multiple Sorcerers, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened, Tzaangors, Chaos Spawn, and Sekhetar Robots, this Grand Coven list is a layered psychic-firepower machine wrapped in a deep infantry shell. 774: Built around Defilers, Forgefiends, Sekhetar Robots, a winged Daemon Prince, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, and half the time Magnus the Red, this is a Hexwarp Thrallband list that floods the board with Daemon Engines and Psychic-tagged melee threats. The win condition is controlling No Man's Land objectives to extend the Flow of Magic across the midfield, then leveraging the Sekhetar Cohort's +1 WS aura from nearby Psykers to crash boosted Sekhetar Robots into whatever the Forgefiends and Enlightened have already softened at range. Armies that can deny its midfield objective control early collapse the Flow of Magic engine, and elite hordes with strong alpha-strike capability can gut the Daemon Engines before the aura synergy goes online.
780: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerers, and Chaos Spawn screening in mass numbers, this Grand Coven list uses the detachment's rotating Command phase abilities — including extended Psychic weapon range and enhanced Psychic shooting — to project overwhelming firepower while flooding the board with bodies. The win condition is layering Psychic shooting from Magnus and Rubric Marines behind a thick Chaos Spawn and Tzaangor screen, using mobile pieces like the winged Daemon Prince and Exalted Sorcerer on Disc to threaten flanks and pressure secondaries. It punishes static gunlines that struggle to chew through horde bodies before the Psychic payoff units get range-extended and into position. It cracks open against elite melee armies that can punch through the screen cleanly and close into Magnus before the Psychic abilities cycle through their one-per-battle uses.
611: Built around Khorne Berzerkers, Jakhals, Exalted Eightbound, Eightbound, Slaughterbound, Chaos Spawn, and Angron delivered inside Chaos Rhinos with Khârn the Betrayer leading the charge, the Berzerker Warband detachment grants every charging unit +1 Attack and +2 Strength on melee weapons — turning an already violent army into a freight train on the turn it contacts. 792: Built around Corsair Voidscarred, Prince Yriel, Corsair Voidreavers, Corsair Skyreavers, Warp Spiders, Striking Scorpions, Lhykhis, Rangers, Shroud Runners, and the Avatar of Khaine, this Eldritch Raiders list weaponizes the detachment's core rule — Anhrathe, Rangers, and Shroud Runners units can Advance and still charge — to flood the board with fast, multi-layered lethal threats from turn one. The win condition is momentum: advance screens and flankers into scoring positions while the Avatar and Voidscarred punch into priority targets, creating kill chains the opponent can't fully address in a single turn. 789: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs led by Lemartes, Sanguinary Priests, and a supporting core of Assault Intercessors and Bladeguard Veterans, this list runs primarily under the Liberator Assault Group detachment, which adds 2 Strength and 1 Attack to all melee weapons on any unit that charged that turn. Opponents who screen effectively to deny charges, or who pack enough anti-infantry firepower to strip the jump pack units before they land, can dismantle the engine before it swings.
788: Built around Sanguinary Guard, multiple squads of Assault Intercessors with jump packs, Death Company Marines with jump packs, Commander Dante, and Lemartes, this is a Liberator Assault Group list that turns every charge into a stat-boosting kill engine — +2 Strength and +1 Attack on all melee weapons after a Charge move. 643: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Terminator Assault Squads, and a Chaplain in Terminator Armour, this is a pure melee avalanche running the Rage-Cursed Onslaught detachment — re-rolling wound rolls of 1 on every melee attack, and adding +1 Attack (or +2 if Battle-shocked) to every charging unit. 791: Built around Death Company Dreadnoughts, Death Company Marines with jump packs, Sanguinary Guard, Lemartes, a jump pack Captain, Intercessors, and Commander Dante, this is a flying melee sledgehammer that exploits charge-triggered attack bonuses — either re-rolling wound rolls of 1 with extra attacks on the charge, or piling on Strength and Attacks simultaneously depending on detachment — to delete priority targets in a single activation. The win condition is using Lemartes to supercharge Death Company Marines into catastrophic charge turns while Sanguinary Guard and Dreadnoughts simultaneously threaten multiple flanks, overwhelming opponents who can only answer one assault vector at a time. It punishes slower melee armies and low-model-count elite lists that cannot screen charge lanes or trade attrition across multiple fronts. It cracks open against heavy shooting armies that can strip the jump pack units mid-approach before the charge lands, neutering the entire attack-bonus engine before it fires.
540: Built around Vindicators, Sanguinary Guard, and Jump Pack Captains buffed by the Angelic Inheritors detachment, this list blends heavy armoured firepower with fast elite melee — an unusual combination that feels more like a mechanised gunline than a classic assault force. Opponents who can neutralise the Vindicators early through long-range anti-tank or who flood the board with enough bodies to absorb the Guard and dilute the charge lanes will crack it open consistently.
648: Built around Defilers, Chosen, Chaos Bikers, Cultist Mobs, and the twin character engine of Abaddon and Huron Blackheart operating inside Pactbound Zealots — which grants Lethal Hits on unmodified 5+ melee rolls across every unit — this is a mobile brawler with genuine anti-armour teeth. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that can't escape melee, as the sheer volume of Lethal Hit fishing overwhelms high-toughness, multi-wound targets. Faster alpha-strike armies or elite shooting forces that delete the screening layer before the brawlers engage can unravel the timing the list depends on.
785: Built around Rotigus, Deathshroud Terminators, a Lord of Contagion, and waves of Beasts of Nurgle, Nurglings, Poxwalkers, Plaguebearers, and Chaos Spawn, this Tallyband Summoners list exploits the detachment's core synergy: Plague Legions daemons sitting within 7" of Death Guard units gain Nurgle's Gift, while Death Guard within 7" of those daemons extend their Contagion Range by 3", creating an interlocking web of attrition across the entire midboard. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot trade efficiently against the sheer volume of durable wounds and cannot escape the expanding contagion aura. Concentrated high-damage shooting or alpha-strike lists that delete key synergy pieces before the web forms can unravel the whole engine before it gets going.
782: Built around Mortarion, Deathshroud Terminators, a Daemon Prince of Nurgle, Foetid Bloat-Drones, and a deep roster of supporting characters running Virulent Vectorium, this list plants Poxwalkers and Chaos Spawn on objectives to trigger the detachment's Afflicted condition while a slow-rolling wall of elite infantry and Defilers grinds forward. 768: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Ghazghkull Thraka, Beast Snagga Boyz, and Boyz packed into Trukks, this is a Freebooter Krew horde that plays as a relentless mid-board brawler — designating a loot objective each Command phase to funnel pressure onto a single priority marker while the mass of bodies contests everywhere else. It punishes slow or fragile armies that can't clear mid-board presence fast enough, drowning them under layers of cheap Gretchin screens, Trukk-delivered threats, and relentless scoring on the loot objective. It cracks against armies that can strip Trukks before disembarkation or hold the mid-board with durable, high-damage units that trade up efficiently against Ork squads.
794: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Vindicators operating under the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment, this list blends armoured firepower with elite melee infantry. Where it cracks is against hyper-mobile or deep-strike-heavy armies that can strip its infantry transports early, leaving the assault core exposed and unable to close without reliable re-roll support.
696: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Ragnar Blackmane, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Blood Claws, Wulfen with Storm Shields, and Intercessor screens, this is a brawling terminator-hammer list running Saga of the Beastslayer, granting Lethal Hits on every attack against Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles army-wide. It punishes opposing lists heavy with Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles by making every swing more lethal into exactly those targets, pressuring expensive models simultaneously across multiple threat vectors. It struggles against cheap, flat infantry hordes that don't trigger the Lethal Hits bonus and can simply drown the elite terminator core in bodies before the kill chain establishes.
776: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened with fatecaster greatbows, Sekhetar Robots, and a deep Sorcerer support stack, Grand Coven floods the board with layered psychic lethality across multiple unit types and ranges. Armies that can strip screens fast and close into melee before Grand Coven cycles its abilities will crack the tempo, and the build's footprint makes it vulnerable to concentrated alpha strikes that remove key Sorcerer support before the engine activates.
871: Built around Celestian Sacresants, Hospitaller support, Immolators, Paragon Warsuits, Seraphim, Zephyrim, and a dense command structure of Morvenn Vahl, Canonesses, and Junith Eruita, this is a mobile infantry swarm that floods the board from transports and the air. High-damage alpha strikes that strip the Immolators before they deliver their cargo, or shooting that outranges the entire force, can collapse the tempo before the beatdown gets started.
718: Built around Dominion Squads ferried in Immolators, Castigators, Paragon Warsuits, Morvenn Vahl, Exorcists, Retributors, Seraphim, and a jump-pack Canoness, the Bringers of Flame detachment turns every ranged weapon into an Assault weapon and spikes Strength by 1 within 6" — rewarding aggressive, point-blank positioning from transports. It cracks under pressure from fast deep-strike threats and aggressive melee that disrupt the precise disembarkation timing the strength buff depends on, leaving Dominions stranded short of the 6" sweet spot.
438: Built around Kastelan Robots managed by Cybernetica Datasmiths, Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, and a dense supporting core of Tech-Priest Enginseers, Skitarii Rangers, Servitor Battleclades, Onager Dunecrawlers, Skorpius Disintegrators, and Ironstrider Ballistarii under the Cohort Cybernetica detachment — boosting every Legio Cybernetica unit +2" Move and +1 OC while not Battle-shocked. It punishes armies relying on vehicle-heavy gunlines by combining mobile anti-armour firepower with resilient, high-OC objective holders that are genuinely costly to remove. Battle-shock effects crack this list open — drop the robots' OC and movement advantage simultaneously and the engine stalls hard.
632: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, and a dense mass of Sicarian Ruststalkers, Sicarian Infiltrators, Ironstrider Ballistarii, and Skitarii Rangers, this list floods the table with layered infantry supported by fast mobile elements. It punishes horde and mid-density infantry armies hard, stacking lethal close-range volleys across multiple waves of cheap bodies that are difficult to remove efficiently. It cracks under pressure from elite alpha-strike lists that can delete the Sicarian packages before they engage, as the army lacks the durability to absorb heavy focused damage without losing its melee engine entirely.
499: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Celestian Sacresants, Castigators, Immolators, and Dominion Squads, this list runs the Sacred Champions detachment to sharpen Sacresants into precision melee threats with boosted BS and WS, while Bringers of Flame turns every short-range gun into an Assault weapon with bonus Strength inside 6". It cracks under pressure from fast alpha-strike armies that can strip the Immolators before delivery and isolate the Sacresants without their support network.
720: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Celestian Sacresants, Hospitaller support, Paragon Warsuits, Immolators, Castigators, and a broad infantry core, this list runs Army of Faith to squeeze two Acts of Faith per phase out of nearly every unit, with Sacred Champions layering +1 BS and WS onto the Sacresants to make them a precision melee hammer. It punishes mid-range infantry-heavy lists by drowning them in skimmer-delivered flamer and melee volume that's nearly impossible to screen against efficiently. Where it cracks is against elite armies that can strip its relatively fragile transports early, collapsing the delivery system before the Acts of Faith engine pays off.
807: Built around Belisarius Cawl, massed Kataphron Breachers and Destroyers, Tech-Priest Manipuli, Servitor Battleclades, and Sicarian Infiltrators flooding mid-board with Skitarii Rangers and Vanguard screening, this is a layered horde-gunline running primarily Lords of the Forge, which gives Tech-Priests a 4+ invulnerable save, Feel No Pain 5+, and the Baffling Data Screed ability to strip enemy vehicle actions. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear waves of cheap screening infantry before the Kataphron killboxes come online. It cracks open when faced with aggressive alpha-strike pressure that collapses the screening layer early, exposing the slow, expensive Kataphrons before they can fire effectively.
656: Built around Prince Yriel, Lhykhis, the Avatar of Khaine, massed Corsair Voidreavers and Skyreavers, Warp Spiders, Rangers, Shroud Runners, and Fire Prisms, this is a mobile, layered Aeldari force that blends fast skimmer shooting with disposable infantry waves across multiple detachments. It punishes lists that rely on slow, expensive elite infantry by bleeding mortal wounds through the Corsair Coterie's objective-zone hazard and overwhelming the opponent's ability to prioritise targets across a wide horde footprint. It struggles against fast, aggressive armies that can bypass the objective-zone mortal wound trap early, strip the fragile Corsair screening units, and isolate Yriel and the Avatar before their melee threat can be delivered.
812: Built around Windriders, War Walkers, Warlock Skyrunners, Farseer Skyrunners, and Shroud Runners, this is a fast, vehicle-heavy Aeldari force running Armoured Warhost and Windrider Host together, giving every vehicle Assault on its ranged weapons while holding the bike cavalry in reserve to arrive a round early. It punishes slower, static armies that struggle to contest midboard objectives against persistent, highly mobile screens arriving in waves. However, it folds to volume-fire lists that can strip Windriders efficiently before the reserve wave stabilizes, leaving objective hold paper-thin.
793: Built around Eldrad Ulthran, Warlock Conclaves, Warlock Skyrunners, Rangers, Fire Dragons with Fuegan, War Walkers, Warp Spiders, Dark Reapers, and Storm Guardians, this list runs Path of the Outcast alongside the Seer Council's Fate dice engine to layer psychic support across an aggressive, skimmer-heavy force. The plan is to exploit the Rangers' detection-boosting shoot trigger to flush hidden or screened units into the open, then delete them with concentrated fire from War Walkers and Dark Reapers while Fuegan's Fire Dragons handle armour and Warp Spiders reposition to contest objectives. Armies that can flood the board early and deny skimmer lanes, or apply hard alpha-strike pressure before the psychic and detection synergies come online, can disrupt the fragile setup this list depends on.
576: Built around a full suite of Aspect Warriors — Howling Banshees, Warp Spiders, Swooping Hawks, Dire Avengers, Striking Scorpions, Fire Dragons, and the Avatar of Khaine, led by named Phoenix Lords Jain Zar, Lhykhis, Fuegan, and Asurmen — this is an Aspect Host list that fields nearly every shrine simultaneously. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb simultaneous multi-vector threats from fast, mobile units with stacked re-rolls. 655: Built around Eldrad Ulthran, multiple Warlock Conclaves, Farseers, and War Walkers, this list runs Armoured Warhost as its foundation — giving War Walkers Assault on all ranged weapons — layered with Seer Council's Fate dice engine in two-thirds of lists to manipulate Stratagems. 809: Built around Warlock Conclaves, Eldrad Ulthran, Farseers, and War Walkers supported by Storm Guardians, Rangers, Fire Dragons, Howling Banshees, and Warlock escorts, this is a dense psychic-command horde that blends elite strike elements with cheap bodies across multiple detachments — most commonly Seer Council or Fateful Performance, occasionally Guardian Battlehost or Path of the Outcast. 577: Built around mass Windrider squads, Warlock Skyrunners, Shroud Runners, War Walkers, Rangers, and Shining Spears, with Eldrad Ulthran and Farseer Skyrunners providing psychic layering, this is a fast, wide skimmer swarm operating primarily through Path of the Outcast and Windrider Host — the latter letting Asuryani Mounted and Vyper units arrive from Reserves a full round earlier than normal. 585: Built around Bullgryn Squads, Commissars, Tech-Priest Enginseers, Hellhounds, and Scout Sentinels, this list uses the Abhuman Auxiliaries detachment to extend Commissar Orders onto its Bullgryn and Ogryn units while running a heavy gunline backstop with mobile anti-armour pressure. 856: Built around Spiritseers, Wraithguard, Wraithblades, Wraithlords, Warlock Skyrunners, and Rangers, this list runs Spirit Conclave and Armoured Warhost to fuse a slow Wraith infantry core with mobile skimmer fire support. 811: Built around Wraithlords, Wraithguard, Wraithblades, and Spiritseers running the Spirit Conclave detachment, this list floods the board with Wraith Constructs guided by Asuryani Psykers — Eldrad Ulthran and Warlock Skyrunners providing mobile psychic support across the force. 818: Built around Kasrkin, Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, Scout Sentinels, Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks, Lord Solar Leontus, Chimeras, Gaunt's Ghosts, and a Tech-Priest Enginseer, this list uses the Designation Force detachment — where Scout Sentinels and infantry smoke units gain Signal Flares — to paint targets and unleash a layered gunline backed by heavy armour. 663: Built around Cadian Shock Troops, Death Korps of Krieg, Kasrkin, Tempestus Scions, Scout Sentinels, and a Rogal Dorn Commander, this is a classic layered gunline running Combined Arms to blanket the board in bodies and barrels. 547: Built around Tech-Priest Enginseers keeping multiple Titanic vehicles operational, Scout Sentinels throwing Signal Flares to designate targets, and Baneblades and Baneswords as the primary damage dealers, with Lord Solar Leontus and Gaunt's Ghosts rounding out the command layer. It punishes armies built around durable, high-wound elites by stacking multiple Titanic guns into the same marked target and leveraging the Engine Speaker and Titan Killer enhancements to maximise that kill chain. It cracks apart when fast, high-volume melee threats lock up its superheavies before they can reposition, since the entire engine depends on keeping those vehicles alive, mobile, and at range.
548: Built around Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Leman Russ Exterminators, Rogal Dorn Commanders, and Hellhounds, with Tempestus Scions, Tempestus Aquilons, Scout Sentinels, and Cadian Shock Troops rounding out the force under Bridgehead Strike. It punishes elite-light armies that lack anti-tank overload by drowning them in durable vehicles that require more firepower to remove than they typically carry. It cracks open against high-volume anti-tank spam or alpha-strike lists that can strip the armoured core before the Scions' drop amplifies output enough to matter.
837: Built around Sword Brethren, Marshals, Castellans, the Emperor's Champion, Repulsor Executioners, High Marshal Helbrecht, Crusader Squads, and Scout Squads, this is a combined-arms Black Templars force blending heavy armoured firepower with aggressive melee infantry. 583: Built around Kasrkin, Cadian Shock Troops, and Chimeras supported by a dense officer corps of Cadian Castellans and Command Squads, this is a mechanised gunline that floods the table with Orders-buffed infantry firing from transports and dug-in positions, with Bullgryns providing a close-range anvil and Tech-Priest Enginseers keeping vehicles in the fight. 819: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Hellhounds, Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Gaunt's Ghosts, Bullgryns, and Lord Solar Leontus operating under Grizzled Company, this is a mechanised gunline that floods the table with armour, elite infantry screens, and officer-stacked Orders that let every attacking model re-roll hit rolls of 1 while increasing the number of Orders each officer can issue. 817: Built around Hellhounds, a Doomhammer, Scout Sentinels, Bullgryns, and Tech-Priest Enginseers supported by Lord Solar Leontus and Cadian Command Squads, this list runs Abhuman Auxiliaries and Steel Hammer to combine a mobile armoured fist with a grinding super-heavy gunline. 661: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Cadian Shock Troops, Kasrkin, Krieg Combat Engineers, and Rogal Dorn Commanders, all ferried and supported by Tauroxes, with Gaunt's Ghosts providing elite infiltration muscle — this is a deep-order, mass-infantry gunline running Grizzled Company, which boosts Officer Order capacity and grants re-rolls of 1 to hit on all affected units. 475: Built around Assault Intercessors, Crusader Squads, Intercessors, Scout Squads, and Sword Brethren flooding the board alongside Repulsor Executioners providing heavy fire support, with the Emperor's Champion, High Marshal Helbrecht, Marshals, and Castellans layering command buffs throughout — all operating under Bastion Task Force, which lets Adeptus Astartes Battleline units shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back, and perform Actions while doing so. 864: Built around the Emperor's Champion, paired Execrators, Sword Brethren Squads, Crusader Squads, and Repulsor Executioners backed by High Marshal Helbrecht, Crusade Ancients, Castellans, and Scout Squads, all running Companions of Vehemence for army-wide re-rolls on Advance and Charge rolls. 694: Built around multiple Repulsor Executioners supported by Techmarines, Sword Brethren, Castellans, and the Emperor's Champion, this Ironstorm Spearhead list plays a mechanically disciplined heavy gunline that keeps vehicles in the fight through Techmarine repairs and per-phase re-rolls on hit, wound, or damage for every Adeptus Astartes unit. 836: Built around the Emperor's Champion, High Marshal Helbrecht, Repulsor Executioners, Execrators, and Land Raider Redeemers, supported by a deep bench of Crusader Squads, Sword Brethren, Scout Squads, and Intercessors dug into terrain. 669: Built around the Bloodthirster, multiple Lords of Change, Be'lakor, Cultist Mob, Plaguebearers, Flesh Hounds, and Beasts of Nurgle, this is a high-mobility mixed-daemon toolbox running Shadow Legion with near-universal Warptide support — letting Battleline units advance and still charge, turning otherwise passive screening units into sudden mid-table threats. 670: Built around Flesh Hounds, Beasts of Nurgle, Nurglings, Skarbrand, Be'lakor, the Lord of Change, the Great Unclean One, and the Bloodthirster, this is a wide, multi-god daemonic tide running the Daemonic Incursion detachment to redeploy threat from deep strike across the board. 687: Built around War Dog Executioners, Brigands, Karnivores, and Stalkers swarming forward alongside a Knight Ruinator and Knight Abominant, this is a full-warpack assault force running the Helhunt Lance detachment — which lets the Titanic Knights benefit from their own War Dog auras when two or more War Dogs are in range, collapsing the usual big-small unit divide into a unified kill engine. 651: Built around Fabius Bile leading augmented Heretic Astartes Infantry — Possessed, Chosen, Legionaries in Rhinos, Chaos Lords, Mutilators, and screening Cultist Mobs — this is a mass-infantry midboard brawler running the Creations of Bile detachment to buff its footsoldiers with battle-start augmentations. 820: Built around multiple squads of Plaguebearers, Great Unclean Ones, Poxbringers, Beasts of Nurgle, Rotigus, Nurglings, and Sloppity Bilepipers, this is a suffocating Nurgle horde running primarily the Plague Legion detachment to blanket midfield in diseased bodies. 449: Built around Chaos Terminator squads, Kravek Morne, Mutilators, and Cultist Mobs screening them forward, this is a grinding mid-board brawler that wins through attrition and presence rather than finesse. 650: Built around Cultist Mobs, Legionaries, Chosen, Chaos Rhinos, Sorcerers, Warpsmiths, and Chaos Lords, this is a layered mid-table infantry machine running Cabal of Chaos, boosting Psyker shooting through Dark Pact-powered Strength buffs while flooding the board with cheap bodies and elite footsloggers. 524: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and a supporting mass of Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Intercessors, and Scouts, this list runs Wrath of the Rock to make its Adeptus Astartes Infantry and Mounted units dramatically harder to wound — any attack whose Strength exceeds the target's Toughness suffers a -1 to its Wound roll. It punishes mid-table infantry armies that can't screen against both the tank guns and a charge-after-advance threat on the same turn. Anything with reliable anti-tank overload or high-volume mortal wounds strips the Executioners early and collapses the gunline before the melee wave can close.
891: Built around War Dog Huntsmen, Karnivores, Executioners, Stalkers, and Brigands — a swarm of eight to twelve fast, medium-weight Knights flooding every table quarter simultaneously. This build punishes transport-heavy infantry armies hardest, using mobile firepower to crack transports and then pile into the exposed passengers before they can re-screen. Low model count and limited screening options means a tight alpha strike or deep-strike denial game can isolate and delete individual War Dogs before the pack reaches critical mass.
749: Built around War Dog Executioners, Karnivores, and Brigands swarming the board alongside a Knight Abominant, this Hunting Warpack list plays a relentless mobile anti-armour game backed by the Traitoris Lance's extra Dread ability to stack pressure from turn one. The win condition is using the detachment's detection mechanic to strip cover and expose targets, then funneling overlapping shooting and melee kill-chains through the War Dog pack to delete high-value armoured threats while the Abominant anchors a layered damage profile. It punishes transport-heavy infantry armies brutally, with the mobile toolbox of mixed War Dogs threatening every table quarter simultaneously. However, low model count and the Chaos Knights' inherent fragility to concentrated anti-tank fire means a focused alpha strike that removes a few key War Dogs early can unravel the entire scoring engine fast.
882: Built around Cultist Mobs, Noise Marines, Chosen, Legionaries, and Huron Blackheart leading a Masters of the Maelstrom command staff, all riding Chaos Rhinos forward, this is a mass-horde gunline that floods every corner of the board with cheap bodies and mid-range firepower. It punishes low-model-count lists badly — the sheer number of activations overwhelms armies that rely on precise sequencing or thin screens to protect key assets. It cracks against elite close-combat armies that can punch through the Cultist chaff quickly and reach the fragile firepower units before they cycle through enough shooting to matter.
880: Built around Cultist Mobs, Legionaries, Chosen, Chaos Rhinos, a Chaos Lord, Chaos Terminators, and winged Daemon Princes, this is a Cabal of Chaos list that weaponizes Dark Pacts to overcharge its psyker shooting while the Daemon Princes cash in the same ritual mechanic in melee.
