It punishes gunline armies that expect to win trades at distance, because the sheer volume of bodies and layered threat vectors force awkward target priority. It struggles against elite close-range lists that can blow through Cultist screens early and collapse the Rhino wall before the Daemon Princes reach combat.
879: Built around Vashtorr the Arkifane, multiple Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Warpsmiths, Obliterators, and Cultist screens, this is a daemon engine swarm running primarily under Devotees of Destruction, which grants Obliterators' ranged attacks the Heavy keyword for improved accuracy on the move. The plan is to flood mid-table with mobile armoured threats that are individually difficult to prioritize, using Warpsmiths to keep daemon engines functional while Vashtorr supercharges their Dark Pacts, forcing opponents to either concede board control or spread fire too thin. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that lack the volume of anti-armour needed to clear multiple tough vehicles per turn. However, the build struggles against high-mobility alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete daemon engines before Warpsmith repairs come online, and its below-average win rate suggests opponents who can dictate range and tempo crack it open consistently.
878: Built around multiple Librarians (including a Terminator-armoured variant), Azrael, Inner Circle Companions, Deathwing Knights, Sternguard, and Hellblasters, this list runs the Librarius Conclave to pulse a chosen Psychic Discipline across every psyker each round — Divination for re-rolls into hard targets, Pyromancy for volume damage, Biomancy to reposition. The win engine is flexible buffing layered onto a dense gunline: Sternguard and Hellblasters unload under whichever discipline fits the matchup, while Companions and Deathwing Knights punish anything that survives into melee. It excels against slow, heavy-armour lists that can't contest the buff rotation before the shooting dismantles them piece by piece. Armies that apply early pressure across multiple flanks crack it open, forcing suboptimal discipline choices and exposing how expensive and relatively immobile the core is.
874: Built around Rotigus, the Great Unclean One, Beasts of Nurgle, Plaguebearers, Nurglings, Poxwalkers, Deathshroud Terminators, and the Lord of Contagion, this is a Tallyband Summoners list that floods the table with interlocking Plague Legions and Death Guard units to stack Contagion Range bonuses across both halves of the army. The win condition is layered attrition — keeping Plague Legions units within 7" of Death Guard to grant them Nurgle's Gift while simultaneously extending Death Guard Contagion Range, grinding opponents down through compounding passive lethality while Beasts and Deathshroud brawl for mid-table. It punishes slow, durable armies that expect to weather sustained fire, because the density of bodies and passive damage sources overloads reactive strategies. It cracks under alpha-strike pressure and hard anti-armour lists that can isolate and eliminate key Contagion anchor pieces before the synergy web fully assembles.
876: Built around Foetid Bloat-Drones, Defilers, a Lord of Virulence, Poxwalkers, Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Deathshroud Terminators, and supporting characters, this list runs Mortarion's Hammer alongside Paragons of Putrescence to layer Afflicted and Contagion pressure across the entire board from turn one. The win condition is attrition through stacking lethal debuffs — Afflicting distant enemy units each round while extended Contagion Range from Death Guard Characters strips durability off anything in the midfield, letting the mobile anti-armour core of Bloat-Drones and Blight-Haulers clean up weakened targets. It punishes durable, high-toughness armies that expect to weather a grind, since the Afflicted condition degrades their resilience before the shooting phase even begins. However, fast aggressive lists that can close range immediately neutralise the Afflicted selection entirely, collapsing the build's debuff engine before it compounds.
875: Built around Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Foetid Bloat-Drones, Deathshroud Terminators, Lord of Contagion, Lord of Virulence, and Poxwalker screens, this is a mid-range attrition machine that layers Contagion across the board to tag enemies as Afflicted, then punishes that status with mortal wound triggers and elite melee pressure. The win condition is grinding opponents down through stacked Affliction — spreading the debuff via extended Contagion ranges and detachment abilities, rolling mortal wounds in the Command phase, and crashing Deathshroud and blight-haulers into softened targets. It punishes durable infantry and monster-heavy lists that park on objectives, since those multi-wound units accumulate Affliction tokens and bleed mortals every command phase while struggling to remove tanky Death Guard bodies. Highly mobile, elite, single-unit armies — particularly those that avoid combat and pick apart the advance from range — crack it open before Contagion can spread far enough to matter.
877: Built around Sanctus, Reductus Saboteurs, Purestrain Genestealers, Achilles Ridgerunners, Neophyte Hybrids, Acolyte Hybrids, Benefictus, Patriarch, and a wall of supporting bodies, this list runs the Heroes Of The Uprising detachment alongside Purestrain Broodswarm and Xenocult Masses to create a three-engine machine of assassins, swarms, and durable objective holders. The win condition is layered threat saturation: Killer-tagged Sanctus and Saboteurs pick apart characters and exposed units with re-roll-1 hit-and-wound pressure while Purestrains cycle out of combat back into strategic reserves at end of your opponent's Fight phase, then re-threaten next turn, and Neophytes heal 3 wounds per Command phase when sitting inside terrain. It punishes elite low-model-count lists badly — anti-tank gunlines struggle to kill enough bodies fast enough while multiple independent threat vectors demand impossible target prioritisation. Armies with reliable board-wide chip damage or mass mortal wounds crack it open by eroding the horde faster than the healing and reserves cycling can compensate.
885: Built around Immortals and Necron Warriors led by characters under Awakened Dynasty — adding 1 to every Hit roll while a Character leads — and backed by Imotekh, the Nightbringer, Skorpekh Lord, Plasmancers, Royal Wardens, Technomancers, Canoptek Reanimators, and Lokhust Heavy Destroyers. The plan is to grind opponents off objectives through layered reanimation sustained by Reanimators and Technomancers while the Nightbringer and Lokhust Heavy Destroyers provide a credible kill threat that forces opponents to react rather than simply race for points. The boosted Hit rolls across multiple infantry blobs punish medium-armour armies that can't efficiently clear tough, self-repairing blobs before the score gap opens. However, dedicated alpha-strike lists and high-volume high-AP shooting can crack the reanimation loop before it stabilises, and the build's below-par win rate suggests it struggles to close games against top-tier elite armies.
889: Built around Doomsday Arks, Flayed Ones, a Technomancer, Canoptek Wraiths, and the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, this list blends heavy long-range firepower with aggressive melee threats across a spread of detachments — Hand of the Dynasty, Hypercrypt Legion, and Pantheon of Woe all appearing at meaningful rates. The plan is to park Doomsday Arks in protected firing lanes while Wraiths, Flayed Ones, and the Nightbringer pressure mid-board, forcing the opponent to choose between contesting objectives and dealing with lethal melee engagements. It punishes slower, static lists that can't reposition away from the Arks' volume of high-AP fire while simultaneously being overwhelmed in melee. However, its detachment fragmentation means no single game plan is fully optimized, leaving it vulnerable to mobile elite armies that can isolate and delete the Arks before the melee threats arrive.
886: Built around Immortals, Necron Warriors, Plasmancers, Flayed Ones, and Overlords, this list weaponizes the Hand Of The Dynasty detachment's core perk — giving Immortals and Warriors the Assault rule so they can advance and still shoot at full effect, keeping pace with objectives without sacrificing firepower. The win condition is layered board control: advance-and-shoot infantry blocs grind out primary while Flayed Ones pressure flanks, with Hypercrypt Legion's end-of-turn teleport (in over half of lists) repositioning units to contest or deny late. It punishes slow, static gunlines that struggle to shift massed reanimating bodies across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It cracks under pressure from elite alpha-strike armies that can delete infantry blocs before Reanimation Protocols trigger, since the build lacks concentrated heavy hitting to deter aggressive early engagement.
884: Built around Skorpekh Lords, Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, the Nightbringer, the Void Dragon, and Nekrosor Ammentar under Cursed Legion, this is a multi-vector assault force that floods every approach with Destroyer Cult muscle backed by C'tan anchor pieces. The Cursed Legion ability stacks Strength on Destroyer Cult weapons — and escalates further when a unit kills or cripples something — so the plan is to chain kills each turn, converting early contacts into snowballing melee lethality while the C'tan soak return fire and hold ground. It punishes slower, tankier lists by overwhelming their durability with high-Strength melee spam across multiple independent threat vectors simultaneously. Tight, elite combat armies that can alpha-strike key Destroyer units before the kill chain ignites, or shooting lists that can isolate and delete C'tan before they stabilize the line, will crack this build open.
888: Built around Doomsday Arks, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, Nekrosor Ammentar, and supporting characters under Cursed Legion, this is a multi-vector pressure list that hits from every angle simultaneously. The engine is the Cursed Legion Strength escalation chain — once a Destroyer Cult unit destroys or halves an enemy unit, every Destroyer Cult weapon in the army gains a further +2 Strength that turn, turning a single kill into a cascading anti-armour avalanche while Doomsday Arks provide sustained long-range firepower. It punishes elite-heavy and vehicle-dense lists brutally, where the Strength stacking makes even mid-tier Destroyer weapons overkill against multi-wound targets. It struggles against cheap, fast screens that deny the trigger conditions and prevent Ophydian and Flayed One threats from reaching priority targets cleanly.
858: Built around the Nightbringer, Void Dragon, Deceiver, and Transcendent C'tan alongside Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers, this list fields a murderer's row of near-unkillable demigods backed by elite melee infiltrators. The plan is to flood the mid-table with Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers applying relentless close-range pressure while the C'tan constellation bulldozes whatever threatens to hold ground, converting raw combat power into primary and secondary scoring simultaneously. It punishes armies built around elite, high-value targets by overloading threat saturation — no opponent can remove four C'tan-tier pieces in the same turn, making efficient sequenced killing nearly impossible. It cracks against armies with hard board presence early enough to deny the infiltrators their positioning, or high-volume chip damage that grinds the C'tan down before they can deliver.
890: Built around Lokhust Lords buffing Lokhust Destroyers and Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers as a melee threat, Nekrosor Ammentar as a force multiplier, and Canoptek Reanimators keeping the killing units alive, with the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon as a durable mid-table anchor. The list wins by pushing Destroyer firepower into contested objectives — roughly a third of lists run Starshatter Arsenal to add +1 to hit on objectives and grant Assault to vehicle and mounted ranged weapons, turning the mobile Destroyer core into a scoring engine that punishes opponents for holding ground. It excels against mid-weight elite infantry and vehicle lists that can't trade efficiently into Reanimation-backed Destroyers, especially when Ophydians pin down backfield threats. Armies with high-volume mortal wound output or enough anti-tank overload to strip the C'tan and heavy Destroyers before Reanimation triggers will crack the attrition engine apart.
895: Built around Gretchin screens, Stormboyz, Deffkoptas, Warbikers, Boyz, and Wazdakka Gutsmek, this is a Taktikal Brigade list that floods the table with cheap bodies and fast melee threats across every wave. The plan is to use Gretchin to lock down midfield objectives while Stormboyz — granted Battleline by the detachment — and Warbikers crash into the enemy lines, keeping infantry eligible to start actions even after advancing or falling back to stack primary score relentlessly. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that can't realistically kill through the sheer replacement volume of a multi-wave horde running layered lethality in melee. High-mobility alpha lists and anything that generates enough mortal wounds or blast weapons to thin screens before the swarm arrives will crack it wide open.
893: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Vindicators, and Scout screening units running the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment, this list plays a grinding mid-table brawl backed by heavy demolisher fire. It punishes elite infantry-light lists that cannot absorb repeated demolisher blasts and lack the bodies to trade into Terminator blobs efficiently. It cracks open against high-volume mortal-wound output or long-range anti-tank that can suppress the Vindicators before the melee core closes distance.
894: Built around Logan Grimnar, Wolf Guard Terminators, Terminator Assault Squads, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and dual Librarians (one in Terminator armour), this is a terminator-heavy mid-board brawler that floods the table with heavily armoured bodies under rotating psychic buffs — most lists run Librarius Conclave, cycling Divination for rerolls or Biomancy for extra threat range each round. The plan is to crash a wall of terminators into the mid-table, use Logan and the Battle Leader to amplify melee output, and grind opponents off objectives through sheer staying power and combat attrition. It punishes horde and elite infantry lists that lack the concentrated anti-tank volume needed to delete multi-wound Terminator blobs before they close, especially when Celerity or Encircling Jaws push charge ranges dangerously far. Dedicated gunlines or armies with consistent high-AP shooting at range can crack it by stripping Terminators in the movement phase before the melee engine ever engages.
896: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, supported by Forgefiends, Sekhetar Robots, Rubric Marines, Chaos Spawn screens, and Tzaangor bodies flooding the midboard, this is a mass-horde brawler with a heavy gunline backbone. The plan is to saturate objectives with expendable Tzaangors and Spawn while the Terminators and Forgefiends threaten from range and punch through anything that contests, using sheer volume of bodies and psychic firepower to grind opponents off the board. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that lack the volume to clear multiple waves of cheap screening units while simultaneously answering the ranged threat of the Robots and Forgefiends. It struggles against fast aggressive lists that can isolate and overwhelm the Terminator brick before the screen re-establishes, since the build's midrange durability trades poorly into concentrated alpha-strike pressure.
907: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Sicarian Infiltrators, Ruststalkers, Skitarii Rangers, Servitor Battleclades, Ironstrider Ballistarii, and Skorpius Disintegrators under the Lords Of The Forge detachment — which keeps every Tech-Priest alive with a 4+ invulnerable save, Feel No Pain 5+, and the Baffling Data Screed debuff — this is a mass-infantry swarm that floods the midboard with layered threats while Tech-Priests strip defensive efficiency from enemy vehicles. The win condition is board saturation: transports push infantry onto objectives early, Infiltrators and Ruststalkers brawl for mid-table control, and Ironstriders plus Disintegrators punish anything that can't clear bodies fast enough. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that rely on isolated vehicles, where Data Screed degrades their shooting and the sheer horde volume overwhelms their damage output. It cracks against high-volume mortal wound output or heavy blast weapons that erase squads wholesale before the midboard brawl can be established.
954: Built around Mortifiers (averaging nearly three squads), Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, and Castigators, this list combines hard-hitting melee penitent engines with a dense firebase of Immolators and Castigator tanks to project threat across the entire board. The win condition is attrition through simultaneous pressure — Mortifiers crash forward into backline targets while Immolators and Castigators saturate mid-board with skimmer-mounted firepower, creating impossible trade decisions for the opponent. Hallowed Martyrs rewards the engine by making damaged Mortifier units hit and wound more reliably the deeper they've taken casualties, so the list actively profits from combat attrition rather than protecting its pieces. It struggles against anything that can shut down the Mortifiers before they engage — long-range alpha-strike armies or deep-strike denial screens that strand the melee core and leave the gunline overexposed.
955: Built around Morvenn Vahl, jump-pack Canonesses, Zephyrim, Seraphim, Paragon Warsuits, and a heavy fire-support backbone of Castigators, Exorcists, and Immolators, this is a full-spectrum Adepta Sororitas list running Army of Faith to squeeze two Acts of Faith per phase out of nearly every unit on the table. The plan is to drown opponents in layered pressure — airborne assault elements crash into mid-board while Castigators and Exorcists hammer armour from range, with Immolators ferrying Battle Sisters and Dominion squads onto objectives. It punishes slower, tankier gunlines that can't handle simultaneous threats from multiple angles, as the mobile elements force reactive positioning while the static guns exact a tax for any overcommitment. Elite deep-strike or alpha-strike lists that can gut the jump-pack core before Acts of Faith compound are the real danger, since losing Morvenn or the Paragons early collapses the anti-armour output this list depends on.
953: Built around Celestian Insidiants, Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Arco-Flagellants, and the Triumph of Saint Katherine, this Hallowed Martyrs list floods the board with transported infantry and fast-moving elite threats backed by layered Character support from Canonesses, Priests, and a Palatine. The engine is deliberate attrition: Hallowed Martyrs' hit and wound bonuses reward taking casualties, so the list absorbs punishment and hits back harder as units drop below starting and half strength, with the Triumph recycling resources to keep the pressure relentless. It punishes mid-density armies that can wound but not wipe units cleanly, since half-crippled Insidiants and Arco-Flagellants simply become more lethal. Highly efficient elite infantry with strong burst damage — particularly big hitters like Custodes or Tau suits — can delete units outright before the martyrdom bonus ever activates, bypassing the core payoff entirely.
908: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Sicarian Infiltrators, Sicarian Ruststalkers, Ironstrider Ballistarii, and a deep bench of Rangers, Marshals, Serberys Raiders, Servitor Battleclades, and Tech-Priest Manipuli — primarily running Haloscreed Battle Clade — this is a mass-infantry swarm that floods the midboard with layered bodies while cycling Halo Override buffs across key units each Command phase. The win condition is attrition-by-volume: Infiltrators and Ruststalkers brawl for mid-table control while Ballistarii provide mobile anti-armour pressure and Rangers hold flanks, collectively generating enough bodies-on-objectives to outscore opponents over multiple rounds. It punishes lists that rely on concentrated shooting to clear objectives, because replacing one screened unit with another from a deep horde is a math problem opponents run out of answers to. It cracks open against elite alpha-strike armies that can surgically delete the key mid-table pieces before Halo Override can cycle, collapsing the layered lethality engine before it gets rolling.
857: Built around Spiritseers, Wraithguard, Wraithlords, Wraithblades, Rangers, Eldrad Ulthran, and the Avatar of Khaine, this list runs the Spirit Conclave detachment to create a lethal feedback loop: when enemy units destroy your Asuryani Psykers, they earn Vengeful Dead tokens, and every subsequent Wraith Construct attack against that unit gains +1 to hit and wound simultaneously. The plan is to bait psyker kills early, then detonate the token payoff through massed Wraith Construct attacks that threaten to delete anything they reach, while Rangers screen objectives and anchor board presence. It punishes elite low-model-count armies hardest — a single token on a key unit means your Wraithguard and Wraithblades are hitting and wounding on 2s, making expensive targets catastrophically vulnerable. Horde armies and lists that can bypass or ignore the psyker kill condition will blunt the token engine and force the Wraith Constructs to fight at base efficiency, where their mobility limitations become a serious liability.

926: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Hellhounds, Scout Sentinels, Leman Russ Exterminators, Leman Russ Battle Tanks, and Cadian Shock Troops, this is a mobile armoured gunline that floods the board with Squadron vehicles across Abhuman Auxiliaries and Steel Hammer detachments. 928: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Kasrkin, Gaunt's Ghosts, Krieg Combat Engineers, Cadian Shock Troops, a Rogal Dorn Commander, Cadian Command Squads, and Taurox transports running Grizzled Company, this list layers elite deep-striking infantry over a massed mobile gunline. 927: Built around Bullgryns, Gaunt's Ghosts, Rogal Dorn Commanders, Attilan Rough Riders, and a Commissar-anchored infantry screen, this Grizzled Company list layers a heavy gunline behind hard-hitting melee and infiltrating specialist units. It struggles against fast, high-volume alpha-strike lists that can collapse the screen before Orders come online and isolate the Bullgryns without support.
929: Built around Krieg Combat Engineers, Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Krieg and Catachan Heavy Weapons Squads, Cadian Recon Squads, Scout Sentinels, and a broad infantry horde, this is a Designation Force list that uses Signal Flares to paint targets for massed ranged firepower across every range band. 925: Built around Hellhounds, Rogal Dorn Commanders, Leman Russ Exterminators, Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Scout Sentinels, and Tech-Priest Enginseers under the Bridgehead Strike detachment, this is a mobile armoured column that floods the board with Squadron vehicles and keeps them alive through sustained repairs. Concentrated anti-tank overload from elite vehicle-hunting lists can strip its repair loop faster than Enginseers can compensate, leaving the armoured core exposed and outgunned.
932: Built around Bullgryn Squads, a Doomhammer, Tech-Priest Enginseers, and Lord Solar Leontus, this list runs the Abhuman Auxiliaries and Steel Hammer detachments — pairing armoured abhuman infantry with superheavy firepower kept battle-ready by constant repairs. Harder armies that can alpha-strike the superheavy or park durable elite melee into the Bullgryns before they engage will crack the list open, since losing the Doomhammer early collapses the anti-armour engine entirely.
913: Built around Death Company Marines with jump packs, Chaplain with jump pack, Death Company Dreadnoughts, Lemartes, Sanguinary Guard, and a Captain with jump pack, this is a multi-wave jump infantry assault force with Intercessors anchoring home objectives. The win condition is overwhelming melee pressure delivered by multiple independent jump-capable threats simultaneously — Lemartes supercharging Death Company while Sanguinary Guard and Dreadnoughts hit adjacent flanks, making it nearly impossible to triage defensively. It punishes slower elite armies by flooding contact points faster than they can respond, with enough mobile anti-armour to threaten vehicles that would otherwise weather the storm. It cracks against heavy shooting gunlines and dense screens that deny charge lanes, since losing momentum early leaves the Intercessors holding objectives alone with no meaningful counter-attack.
916: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Commander Dante, Death Company Marines with jump packs, and double Vindicators, this list pairs a hard-hitting jump infantry core with heavy demolisher cannon fire. The plan is to use Vindicators to crack open armoured targets and clear blobs from range while Sanguinary Guard and Death Company — frequently benefiting from charge-after-Advance through Stormlance — crash into mid-board objectives and delete whatever survives. It punishes static gunlines and infantry-dense armies that can't withstand simultaneous pressure from deep-striking melee hammers and 6" blasts. Opponents who can screen out the jump infantry charges or apply consistent anti-tank to strip the Vindicators early will dismantle both halves of the engine before they can coordinate.
918: Built around multiple Baal Predators, Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with jump packs, a Captain with jump pack, Commander Dante, Lemartes, and Chief Librarian Mephiston, this list runs the Liberator Assault Group detachment to blend fast armour with a charging elite infantry package. It cracks when facing elite long-range shooting or fast alpha-strike armies that deny the 12" window before the kill chain assembles.
